articleTitle: A Dual Loop Low-Dropout Regulator with Fast Transient Response
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this work, a dual loop low-dropout regulator (LDO) with fast transient response is proposed to provide a clean supply for mixed-signal system. The proposed LDO has a high-speed inner loop for enhancing transient response capability, and the global loop has high gain to improve the power supple rejection (PSR). The circuit is designed and simulated in 28nm CMOS process, including 50pF on chip load capacitor. For a 1. 8V input voltage and 0. 9V output voltage, the simulated undershoot and overshoot voltage is only 60mV and 48. 5mV, respectively, for load transient of 0μA to 10mA within edge times of 120ps. The PSR is 43dB at lMHz and is better than 19dB through up to 10GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: 2-6GHz 30W GaN Power Amplifier Using Reactive Matching Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact 2-6 GHz power amplifier (PA) MMIC utilizing Sanan’s 0.25-$\mu$m gallium nitride high-electron-mobility transistor (GaN HEMT) technology. The design focuses on implementing the output matching network (OMN). Meanwhile, the reactive matching (RM) technique and direct parallel power combiners are employed to reduce power loss and chip area in this PA. Under a drain voltage of 28 V, the GaN PA achieves an average output power (Pout) of 45 dBm (31W) and an average power gain of 19 dB, with a power-added efficiency (PAE) ranging from 27% to 40% over the entire bandwidth. The proposed chip has an area of $4.5\times 3.4$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and an average power density of 5 W/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Corrosion Behavior Analysis and Panel Properties Protection in Flexible OLEDs
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Flexible organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) are of increasing attention to improve the flexibility of wearable and foldable displays. However, the inevitable issues like electrochemical corrosion due to high temperature-high humidity and operating state is causing serious concern. In this paper, we have discussed the electrochemical corrosion behaviors in flexible OLEDs and presented the formation mechanism systematically. The focused-ion-beam (FIB) pictures show puffy metal reaction resultant and adhesive peeling appearance, which made passageways between the two adjacent trace lines in panel and caused electric short. To address the electrochemical corrosion concern, several techniques were presented for panel properties protection, including interface adhesion improving, ultraviolet rays (UV) hard baking and passivation layer coating. It was demonstrated that the suppression of puffy metal and the elimination of adhesive peeling were obtained after high temperature-high humidity experiments. The research opens the possibility of considering more influences on reliabilities improvements in flexible OLEDs.

articleTitle: Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm Based Parameter Extraction Method for GaN HEMT on Si and SiC Substrates
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an enhanced small-signal model for GaN HEMTs that accurately characterizes the behavior of GaN HEMT on Si and SiC substrates. The model incorporates novel parameters to simulate the substrate/buffer loading effect observed in Si substrates due to lattice mismatch induced defects. An improved Whale Optimization Algorithm base on local perturbation and nonlinear convergence factor (PNC-WOA) is proposed to determine the optimal values of the model extrinsic elements. A very good agreement with measurements is achieved when using the improved small-signal model and PNC-WOA, validating its applicability for GaN HEMT on Si and SiC substrates.

articleTitle: UVM-based Reusable Hardware Accelerator Verification Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: We design a UVM-based reusable hardware accelerator verification platform to better verify increasingly complex hardware accelerator designs. The verification platform mainly uses coverage-driven convergence technology, combined with directional testing and constrained random excitation, to perform functional verification on the IP in the multi-core accelerator chip. The verification environment is built according to the verification requirements of the convolutional neural network hardware accelerator, and the data flow control functions such as convolution, activation, pooling, and fully connected function layers in the design and the base address and data offset are verified. Verify existing hardware accelerator, the experimental results prove that the verification platform quantifies the verification progress according to the mechanism in UVM to ensure the verification completeness of the functional modules; In addition, the accelerator verification platform of the network model of different structural layers can be reused with a small amount of modification, which shortens the verification cycle.

articleTitle: Fast transient response enhancement circuit for LDO
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a fast transient enhancement circuit for LDO is proposed. This structure improves the problem of overshoot and undershoot voltage and long stability time when the traditional LDO loads are transient. The push-pull amplifier structure is introduced to double the charging and discharging current of the power transistor when the transient state changes. In addition, the two currents of the push-pull amplifier can be duplicated by making use of the replicable characteristics of the two branches of the amplifier, and the subtraction operations of in-phase and inverse phase are performed respectively, so as to control the opening and closing of the two transient enhancement circuits. Since the transient enhancement current is copied by the current mirror, the magnitude of the transient enhancement current can be controlled to a certain extent. Under the typical load switching state, the proposed scheme can control the overshoot voltage within 35mV and the undershoot voltage within 24mV. Compared with the traditional LDO structure, the overshoot voltage and undershoot voltage are increased by 84% and 77% respectively, and the recovery time of overshoot and undershoot is increased by 30% and 32% respectively.

articleTitle: An RF Power Amplifier with MGTR and Capacitor Neutralization Technology in 22nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an RF power amplifier for wireless communication devices based on a 22nm CMOS process. The main circuit is designed based on a pseudo-differential cascode structure, which amplifies the differential-mode signal while improving the tolerance of the circuit. Multigated transistor (MGTR) technology is used to improve linearity and back-off efficiency while capacitor neutralization (CN) technique is employed to enhance the stability. Simulated results show that the saturation output power is 31.03dBm with power gain of 25.68 dB and peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 49.02%. Meanwhile, the PAE at 6dB/9dB/12dB power back-off point is obtained as 27.00%/17.22%/10.18%, and the output 1dB compression power is 29.72dBm.

articleTitle: A 32 Gb/s NRZ PI-Based Baud-Rate Digitial Clock and Data Recovery Circuit in 28nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The paper presents a novel baud rate Clock Data Recovery (CDR) architecture with a maximum rate of 32Gb/s based on a time-interleaved ADC-based Serdes designed in the 28nm process. The paper discusses the architectural details of the CDR, including the use of MMPD for early and late judgments, the design of the proportional-integral branch and the octagonal PI with 128 phases. It also analyzes the linearized model of the CDR and estimates the jitter tolerance. The simulation results show that the proposed CDR design effectively recovers the clock and maintains a stable BER at a data rate of 32Gb/s, while also having good jitter tolerance.

articleTitle: A Highly Reconfigurable 5th Order Active RC Filter for Multi-standard Wireless Receivers in 12-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a highly reconfigurable receiver (RX) low-pass filter (LPF) with tunable cutoff frequency $\left(f_{o}\right)$ and gain for multi-standard applications. The gain of the designed filter could be tuned from 0 dB to 42 dB by a gain step of 1 dB, whereas the cutoff frequency covers from 0.2 MHz to 100 MHz. The proposed filter is implemented in 12 nm CMOS process. The post-simulation results show that the current consumption is 7.2 mA from 1 V supply and the area occupies $274 \times 238 \mu m^{2}$. The filter achieves 37.3 dBm in-band third-order harmonic intercept point (IIP3). The spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR), signal noise ratio (SNR) and in-band total harmonic distortion (THD) is 74.8 dBc, 96.9 dB and -74.6 dB respectively. The input referred in-band integrated noise (IRN) is $183.2 \mu V_{rms}$.

articleTitle: A 12-bit 625 MS/s Time-interleaved Pipelined ADC
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This article presents a 12-bit 625 MS/s time-interleaved ADC analog-to-digital converter (ADC) that achieves an SFDR/SNDR of 64.47/59.08 dB near Nyquist rate. An input buffer with a replica capacitor is employed to effectively drive the sampling capacitor with high linearity. A bootstrapped sampling switch operating at 625 MS/s is adopted to eliminate timing mismatch and achieve high sampling linearity. Also, the pipelined ADC is utilized as the sub-ADC owing to its balance of sampling rate and revolution. The ADC is implemented in a 45 nm CMOS technology with 376 mW power consumption and a total layout area of 850μm $\times$ 590μm.

articleTitle: Design of Digital Phase Interpolator for 6.25Gbps CDR Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: For high-speed serial interface application, a digital phase interpolator(PI) for 6.25Gbps clock data recovery circuit is designed. The digital PI consisted of two groups of inverter arrays, with a digital signal controlling the number of gating of the inverter array to achieve the phase adjustment function similar to analog PI. Additionally, an 8-phase divider with reset function has been designed to provide 8-phase input clocks with the correct phase relation to the digital PI. The digital PI has been implemented using TSMC 40nm process, with a layout area of 53um*23um Post-simulation results show that, at an operating speed of 6.25 Gbps, the output clock jitter is only 7.66ps, representing less than 0.15 UI, and with a low power consumption of only 0.59 mW.

articleTitle: Design of Millimeter-Wave Asymmetric Single-Pole Double-Throw Switch in a 45nm SOI CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: An asymmetric single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch in a 45-nm silicon-on-insulator (SOI) CMOS process is presented for 5G millimeter-wave (mm-wave) applications. The LC resonant technique and L-/ π -type topology are used to achieve a low insertion loss of less than 0.9 dB in the on-state path and a high isolation of more than 25 dB in the off-state path for 20-34 GHz. At 27 GHz, the 0.1 dB input power compression point for TX and RX paths is 29.1 and 21.0 dBm, respectively. The overall size area of the designed SPDT switch is 0.84 mm * 0.34 mm.

articleTitle: A Low-power, Low-Noise Readout ASIC for Gamma-ray Dosimeter Based on CdZnTe Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to meet the design requirements of portal dosimeters based on Cadmium zinc telluride (CdZnTe) detector, a low power and low noise readout ASIC is proposed in this paper. The power consumption is decreased while the equivalent noise charge (ENC) is not seriously degraded by carefully optimizing the bias current of charge sensitive amplifier. The chip area is 0.127 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding the bias and bandgap circuit. The power consumption of the chip is 1.518 mW at the supply voltage of 3.3 V. The simulated equivalent noise charge(ENC) is about 213.3 e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>. The simulation results show that the non-linear error is 6.32% when the particle energy ranges from 30 keV to 1.5 MeV.

articleTitle: Novel Processes for IR Drop Reducing on the Application of Large Size AMOLED Display
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: We propose a novel process using anode electrode as auxiliary electrode for reduction of VSS drop by exposing the edge of sandwich structure anode layer. In this process flow, an innovative structure is fabricated, which could successfully contact the auxiliary electrodes with top-emission OLED cathode to reduce IR-drop in large size AMOLED display.

articleTitle: Precise Current Sensing Circuit for Li-Battery Power Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A high precision current sense circuit was designed in a 0.18μm BCD IC process and employed in a battery management chip. The influence of offset voltage on current acquisition accuracy is analyzed. The chopper dynamic regulation technology is used to reduce the offset voltage of the amplifier, and the instrumentation amplifier is designed to achieve high precision with a lower detection voltage. The circuit was used in a battery management chip and taped out. The chip test results show that the measurement error of the ADC is less than ±300μV when the input voltage is in the range of −10∼10mV, and the measurement error is less than ± 620μV while the input voltage is in the range of−125∼125mV.

articleTitle: An ASIC Interface for MEMS Vibratory Gyroscopes With a 110 dB DR and 0.001 °s/√Hz Noise Floor Over a 100 Hz
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an ASIC interface for MEMS vibratory gyroscopes with a wide tuning range from 5 kHz to 20 kHz. This ASIC interface integrates a sense open-loop module, a drive close-loop module and mode control circuits. An ultra-high sensitivity and low-power dual chopper amplifier for the signal conditioning of the capacitance-voltage converter and an excellent dynamic range of $110 \mathrm{~dB}$ over a signal band of $100 \mathrm{~Hz}$ analog-to-digital converter are proposed for sense and drive loop detective. The readout interface is fabricated in a 0.18μm BCD technology with an HV-module and OTP. Measurement results indicate that this ASIC interface achieves a noise floor of 0.001 $\circ / \mathrm{s} / \sqrt{ } \mathrm{H z}$ over $100 \mathrm{~Hz}$, a bias stability and a bias instability of $\mathrm{2. 6}$ $\circ / \mathrm{h}$ and $1.05 \circ / \mathrm{h}$, respectively. Moreover, the full-scale range is higher than $\pm 1440 \circ / \mathrm{s}$.

articleTitle: A Dual-Core Digitally Controlled Oscillator with a Switched Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a digitally controlled oscillator (DCO) using novel switched capacitor units. Compared with the traditional switched capacitor unit, the new unit reduces the device stress and improves the quality factor. To further reduce phase noise, the DCO uses a dual-core structure and replaces the traditional tail-current source transistor with a resistor. The proposed DCO is designed in 2Snm process, realizes a phase noise of-110.2dBc/Hz@1MHz at 28GHz, and the frequency modulation range is 27.1GHz-29.2GHz. It consumes 25mW under 0. 9V supply voltage for a figure of merit (FOM) of l85.2dB.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Delay Faults Testing Technique Based on the Improved DWR Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Aiming at the challenge of testing delay faults in through silicon via (TSV) of Chiplets, a high-precision delay faults testing technique based on the improved die wrapper register (DWR) is proposed. Relying on time-to-digital converter (TDC) embedded in the original DWR, transitional signal is propagated in delay chains and conversed into a digital signal to observe whether there is the delay fault. The double delay chains are constructed by two kinds of XOR gates with different delays. The conversion with high precision is achieved by dividing the transition signal into continuous small time-intervals. With the improved test access port controller (TAPC) circuit, the time to configure effective test path is greatly reduced and the delay test can be realized without additional external interfaces. The simulation results demonstrate that delay faults can be detected within the precision of 11.246ps and the time of test configuration is reduced.

articleTitle: ADC Static Test System Based on LabVIEW Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the field of ADC testing, static parameters are parameters that characterize the quantized voltage and the standard quantized voltage of the ADC at certain points in the range. So the measurement of static parameters has always been a research hotspot. The traditional FPGA test method and logic analyzer test method have some problems, such as low accuracy of test results and low data throughput. In this paper, an ADC static parameter test system based on LabVIEW software is proposed. The Slave computer adopts PXI hardware platform, which is fully compatible with LabVIEW, and has great improvement in speed and accuracy. Finally, the simulation of the system and the static test of the 8bit ADC are completed, The measured DNL ranges from 0.12LSB to -0.37LSB, and the INL ranges from 0.45LSB to -0.67LSB.

articleTitle: A Wideband 6-bit Phase Shifter with Low RMS Error in 65nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This letter presents a wideband 6-bit phase shifter with low RMS error in 65nm CMOS technology. Compared with conventional cascode-cascade structure, this active balun utilizes cascode topology, current negative feedback, and symmetrical structure at the same time to minimize phase/amplitude difference and realize stable operation. The three-order RC-CR networks with different resonant frequency generate precise orthogonal signals to control vector adder. The current reference circuit used in DAC gives precise current reference and acts as negative feedback to stabilize the working operation. Digital-to-analog converter(DAC) uses cascode current mirror to copy precise current reference and compensate the phase/amplitude error in the wide band. The experimental result shows that RMS amplitude error and phase error are less than 0.7 dB and 3.2°, respectively, over the bandwidth. The measured return loss is observed better than 9dB from 2 to 18GHz. Its total consumption is 92.4mW under 3.3V supply voltage, and the core chip occupies $600 \mu \mathrm{m} \times 700 \mu \mathrm{m}$.

articleTitle: A 14-ppm/V 1.5-ppm/°C Reference Voltage Source with a Wide Input Range of 4.5-35V
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This work presents a high-precision and wide-input-range reference voltage source based on a 180nm BCD process. The reference voltage source generates a constant voltage of 2.5V under the supply voltage ranging from 4.5V to 35V. Both a pre-regulator with current extraction, and high-order curvature compensation are proposed in this work. The current extraction circuit greatly improves the stability of output voltage, and the high-order term of V$_{\mathbf{BE}}$ in Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT) is used for temperature compensation to achieve an output voltage with a low temperature coefficient. Simulation results show that a line regulation of 14ppm/V is achieved, and an average temperature coefficient is 1.5ppm/°C over the range of −45°C to 125°C. In addition, the Power Supply Rejection Ratio (PSRR) is 102.82dB at 10Hz.

articleTitle: Function-selectable Bitwise Operation Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Bitwise operations have extensive applications in various fields of computer science. However, performing specific-purpose bitwise operations often requires scheduling of Central Processing Unit (CPU) and multiple computation steps of Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), thus the efficiency would undoubtedly decreases when dealing with substantial computational workloads. An acceleration circuit for seven specific bitwise operations is proposed in this paper, aiming to improve the calculation speed of bitwise operations. The simulation verification results shows that the acceleration ratio of the acceleration circuit to ALU exceeds 1.66, confirming the high performance of our deigned circuits in acceleration effect on aspect of bitwise operations.

articleTitle: A 24-28 GHz GaN MMIC Power Amplifier with Filtering Matching Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage power amplifier (PA) monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) for 5G millimeter-wave (mmW) applications using a 0.15 µm GaN-on-SiC technology. To achieve high efficiency and improve gain flatness over a specific operation bandwidth, a synthesized matching strategy with filtering function is adopted. Simulation results show that the realized PA achieves a saturated output power of over 33.5 dBm and a power-added efficiency (PAE) of higher than 32%, with a peak PAE of 36.5% at 26 GHz. The design reveals a small signal gain of 21.0-22.3dB from 24 to 28 GHz, with gain flatness of ±0.6 dB. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed MMIC for 5G mmW systems.

articleTitle: A low-noise and low-power front-end readout ASIC for CZT detectors
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A low-noise and low-power front-end readout ASIC for CZT detectors has been designed and implemented in this work. This front-end readout ASIC has the characteristics of low noise, large input range, high accuracy and low power consumption, and is especially suitable for portable X/γ-ray spectrometers. The ASIC has been implemented using a $0.18\mu\mathrm{m}$ CMOS process. The test results indicate that, the input energy range is 0~8fC, the nonlinearity of gain is less than ±6%, the equivalent noise charge (ENC) for zero capacitance is only $147\mathrm{e}^{-}$, and the static power consumption is less than 2.5mW/ channel.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Image Processing Platform Based on GUI
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Image processing technology covers a wide range of application fields, with in-depth research on various image theories, technologies, equipment, and a wide range of research fields. In order to facilitate researchers to visually and quickly analyze the effectiveness of relevant algorithms, an image processing simulation platform is designed using a GUI visual interaction interface. The design principles and processes are conceptualized, and the overall design of the platform is constructed. The functions of each sub interface are implemented based on the division of modules. The processing effects of different algorithms can be compared visually through running the results, and the application of image processing technology in license plate recognition can be demonstrated through comprehensive examples Comprehensive application in smart classroom attendance process. The test results of the simulation platform indicate that the image processing platform is easy to operate and expand, effectively assisting operators in deepening their understanding and application of image processing technology.

articleTitle: Design of a High-Performance Power Supply Module with Subsection Compensation BGR and Capless LDO for Chip Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A high-performance power supply module for chip applications is presented in this paper using 180nm CMOS technology. The module includes a subsection compensation bandgap reference (BGR) and a capless low-dropout regulator (LDO) to address low temperature drift and low load adjustment (LDR) challenges. The temperature coefficient (TC) of the power supply module output voltage can be reduced using the subsection compensation technique. Additionally, the capless LDO with transient enhancement ensures proper functionality of the power supply module within the chip. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed power supply module achieves a TC lower than 3 ppm/K, LDR lower than 0.002%, and overshot and undershot voltage lower than 400 $\mu$V, confirming its effectiveness in meeting low temperature drift and low load adjustment rate requirements.

articleTitle: An Output-Capacitor-less LDO with Push-pull Stage and Transient-enhanced Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This article presents an output capacitor-less low dropout regulator (LDO) that achieves fast transient response through a current compensation circuit. The push-pull structure improves the voltage swing rate at the gate of the pass device and enables the gate capacitor to quickly charge and discharge when switching between light and heavy loads. The current compensation circuit is composed of logic-threshold trigged comparator (LTTC) circuit and replication transistor. When the output voltage changes, the logical threshold voltage of LTTC will change, so as to achieve the effect of comparison, to open or turn off the replication transistor, and can compensate the output current to stabilize the output voltage. The proposed structure has been implemented in CMOS 0.1S-$\mu$m standard process. The measured voltage undershoot and overshoot is 192mV and 190mV respectively with a load steps from 10$\mu$A to 500mA with 500ns edge times.

articleTitle: Adaptive Resistance Calibration Circuit for High-speed Serial Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This work presents an adaptive resistance calibration circuit for high-speed serial transceivers. The structure of the circuit includes resistance calibration unit, amplifier, current mirror, comparator and adaptive algorithm unit. The resistance calibration circuit proposed in this work can accurately adjust the driving impedance of the transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) in high-speed serial transceivers. Then, by comparing with the external resistance, the proposed circuit can ensure that the total resistance in the resistance calibration unit is consistent with the external one. In this way, the design can effectively avoid the influence of resistance error caused by temperature and process deviation, so as to ensure impedance matching. In summary, all principles and simulation results of the adaptive resistance calibration circuit are presented in detail in this work.

articleTitle: Compact MEMS-Based Computational Mid-Infrared Spectrometer on Silicon-on-Insulator Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Microspectrometers have been rapidly developed in the past few years due to their advantages of compact footprint, low cost, and in-situ measurement capability. The mid-infrared (MIR) has received great attention as a key band in spectroscopic sensing. However, the development of compact and high-performance MIR microspectrometer is still in its infancy. Here, we present a MEMS-based on-chip computational MIR microspectrometer that uses an in-plane comb-drive actuator to modulate a directional coupler built on the most common silicon-on-insulator platform. The in-plane comb-drive actuator can break through the limitation of photolithography resolution to reduce the waveguide coupling spacing, enhance the coupling strength, and increase the optical path difference, thereby improving the resolution and the compactness of the spectrometer. A spectral resolution of 3 nm and a bandwidth of 300 nm ($4-4.3 \mu \text{m})$ are achieved within a compact footprint of100 $\times 1000\mu \text{m}^{2}$.

articleTitle: Design of Nonlinear Phase Frequency Detector and Low Mismatch Charge Pump
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a nonlinear phase frequency detector (PFD) and a low-mismatch, wide-swing charge pump (CP) based on a 22nm CMOS process. Based on D flip-flop structure, the phase frequency detector adopts TSPC D flip-flop structure to realize nonlinear phase discrimination. The charge pump adopts the linear current mirror structure to expand the output voltage range. The high gain input rail to rail amplifier improves the matching accuracy of charge and discharge current. The current of CP can be adjusted by using 6bit control word. The simulation results show that the phase detection range of PFD is (-1.97π, 1.97π). The static current mismatch of CP is less than 0.1% and the output voltage range is 0.1-0.9V. The power consumption of PFD&CP is 0.7mW at 100μA current mode.

articleTitle: A 12-bits 100 MSPS Current-Steering DAC With Low-Power In 40nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents the design and investigation of a 12-bit high-precision low-power digital-to-analog converter (DAC) based on TSMC 40nm CMOS technology. The proposed DAC architecture is a current-steering type, which employs a 5 most significant bits (MSBs), 4 middle LSBs (MLSBs), and 3 least significant bits (LSBs) decoding segments, operating at a sampling rate of 100 million samples per second (MSPS). The overall circuitry comprises reference circuits, switch driving circuits, decoding circuits, and current source arrays. The performance of the DAC circuitry is evaluated through the simulation of static and dynamic error indicators using Cadence Spectre. The simulation results indicate that the proposed DAC exhibits excellent static performance with differential non-linearity (DNL) of ±0.12 LSB and integral non-linearity (INL) of ±0.18 LSB. Additionally, the DAC demonstrates low static power consumption of approximately 9.7 mW. The dynamic performance of the DAC is evaluated in terms of effective number of bits (ENOB) and spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR), which are estimated to be 11.92 bits and 81 decibels of carrier (dBc) at 100 MHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Research Progress of Electrospinning Nanofibers
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Nanofibers play an important role in the field of flexible electronic devices. Electrospinning is a simple and universal technology for preparing ultrafine fibers. However, conventional electrospinning nanofibers are often disordered, which limits their applications in devices that require an array or patterned fiber structure. In this paper, electrospinning is reviewed from the aspects of principle, material, characterization and influencing factors. The optimization method of electrospinning device proposed by researchers in recent years is introduced. The applications of electrospinning and electrospinning nanofibers in flexible electronic devices are summarized. At the same time, the deficiency of electrospinning research and its future development trend were also discussed.

articleTitle: A 0.0025mm2 8-bit 70MS/s SAR ADC with a Linearity-Improved Bootstrapped Switch for Computation in Memory
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Resistive Random Access Memory (ReRAM)-based analog computing-in-memory (CIM) is a promising approach to tackle the memory wall problem in data-intensive operations. However, in ReRAM-based analog CIM, the area and energy overhead imposed by DACs and ADCs hinders the potential of CIM. To alleviate this problem, an 8-bit 70 MS/s SAR ADC with a linearity-improved bootstrapped switch and a transconductance-enhanced dynamic comparator is presented in this work. All active devices are placed beneath the capacitors to save the area, resulting in a core area of 0.00255 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in a 110 nm CMOS technology. A proper CDAC switching scheme, transconductance-enhanced comparator, and custom-designed DFF are implemented to improve energy efficiency and speed. Post-layout simulation demonstrates that it achieves 46.22 dB SNDR near Nyquist frequency while consuming 553 uW of power at 1.2 V supply, which yields 47.26 fJ/Conv FoM.

articleTitle: SiC-Based High-Temperature Gate Driver Integrated Circuit for SiC Power MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Silicon carbide materials have great potential for high-temperature applications. SiC-based integrated circuits for high-temperature applications have attracted much attention in recent years. In this paper, a simple SiC-based high temperature gate driver integrated circuit (IC) for SiC power MOSFET is proposed and fabricated. Firstly, the low-voltage SiC CMOS IC process is developed and the electrical performance of the low-voltage CMOS devices is simulated. Then, the gate driver circuit is designed after modeling the BSIM models of the SiC low-voltage CMOS devices. And the proposed SiC gate driver IC consists of level-shift and driver buffer units. The proposed SiC gate driver IC is simulated and the fabricated, and the simulation and experimental results both show that the proposed SiC gate driver IC can be operated in high temperature environments.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Translation System based on Multi-Sensor Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With the development of sensors and integrated circuits, various sensors are used to detect hand gesture motion data for gesture recognition and broadly utilized in multiple sectors. However, there is a shortage of research on dual-hand gesture recognition, as most existing works focus on single-hand gesture recognition. This paper proposes that a hand gesture translation system based on multi-sensor fusion. We develop a simple data glove that utilizes motion sensors and bend sensors to collect gesture information. We compare and improve multiple algorithms commonly used for gesture recognition. We categorize 62 Chinese sign language gestures into four classes and use different algorithms for recognition based on the gesture type, which improves efficiency. In the end, the Euclidean Distance (ED) algorithm was employed for the identification of static sign language, resulting in an average recognition accuracy of 99.42%. Dynamic sign language of both hands is recognized using a CNN+LSTM model, dynamic sign language was recognized with an average accuracy of 98.61%.

articleTitle: A novel readout chip for medical application with high Energy Resolution and high Time Resolution
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A novel readout chip for medical application has been designed and implemented in 180nm HVCMOS technology. It will be used for golden nanoparticles. X rays will be generated by a plasma accelerator. These x-rays will excite the gold atoms that will emit fluorescence photons. These photons can be detected by a hybrid pixel detector with CdTe sensor. There are several novel circuits and concepts. The pixel geometry and bonding pad geometry are different. This allowed very small pixel size for a 180nm technology. The pixel amplifier can cope with both signal polarities. Time to digital converter has been implemented. For energy measurement peak detector has been implemented. The peak detector signal is digitized by a time-based ADC.

articleTitle: A DAC-Based 28Gb/s PAM4 Transmitter for Serial Link System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a DAC-Based transmitter for serial link system. To balance speed and accuracy, the 7b DAC i s divided into 4 binary and 3 thermometer. To improve output impedance matching and reduce return loss, the CML driver is use d in the DAC unit cell. In addition, the quarter-rate 4:1MUX is used in the last stage of multiplexer, which is based on a 1UI pulse generator, reduces the design complexity of the clock circuit. T he DAC-Based TX implements serial 28Gb/s PAM4 output on 65 nm CMOS technology with differential output of 617 mVpp. At t he Nyquist frequency of 6.89GHz, SNDR=38.15dB, SNR=42.01d B, SFDR=40.44dBc, THD=-40.44dB. It consumes 152mW at 1.2 V supply voltage.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient and Robust SNN Classifier for LC-ADC Sampled ECG Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an energy-efficient and robust spiking neural network (SNN) classifier design for level-crossing analog-to-digital converter (LC-ADC) sampled electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. A quantization-aware training method is proposed for the fixed-point quantization stage of the hardware-aware training to achieve better classification accuracy while further compressing the quantization resolution. The SNN classifier is trained with a mixed ECG dataset in which the ECG signals are sampled by LC-ADCs with multiple resolutions. Thus, the robustness of the SNN model is improved, achieving a classification accuracy improvement of up to 2% on various LC resolutions. The classifier is validated on a neuromorphic processor chip and achieves an accuracy of 98.24% with a measured energy consumption of 0.36 $\mu$J/inference. The energy-delay product is 164 pJ$\cdot$s, achieving more than $12 \times$ improvement over other works.

articleTitle: A Programmable Square-Wave Delay Circuit with Self-Calibration Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a programmable square-wave delay circuit with self-calibration structure is proposed, which can keep the rising edge and falling edge delays strictly consistent. It is realized by combining analog and digital circuits, and achieved the benefits of programmable delay time, high accuracy, good linearity and low power consumption. To reduce the delay error caused by the process variations of the capacitor, the self-calibration circuit is applied. And through reusing the rising edge delay path, the rising edge delay and the falling edge delay of the input square wave are strictly the same, which avoids the influence caused by the change of PVT and ensures the constant duty cycle of the input and output square waves. The circuit was designed in the TSMC 65 nm CMOS fabrication process. The simulation results validate that a maximum delay range of 27 ns and a minimum delay step value of 105 ps/LSB can be achieved, which by adjusting the 8-bit delay control signal.

articleTitle: A Low Power OTA-C Filter for Wireless Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The traditional OTA structure uses the current splitting technology to decompose most of the current, which can effectively reduce the transconductance, but the excessive current splitting ratio will bring power loss. To solve this problem, a multiple-output fully differential (MOFD) cascode OTA structure is proposed. This structure can generate additional output by connecting the load to the current splitting branch, which can effectively utilize the current generated by the current splitting to reduce the power loss. In order to reduce the passband attenuation of the filter, the output stage adopts the cascode structure to increase the output impedance of the OTA, and the improved source negative feedback structure obtains lower transconductance and better linear range. Compared with the traditional structure, the number of OTAs of the fifth-order Butterworth low-pass filter with this OTA structure is reduced from 11 to 6, thereby reducing power consumption and achieving lower passband attenuation. The circuit is verified by 0.18 um CMOS process. The results show that the passband gain of the proposed filter is only −6.1 dB. −3dB frequency is 260 Hz. For 100 mV sinusoidal input signal at 50 Hz, the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the filter is about −66 dB and the power consumption is only 11.4 $\mu \mathbf{W}$ at 1.8 V supply.

articleTitle: A multi-cell battery management chip voltage sampling circuit with positive and negative voltage pretreatment structure of the battery
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: There are two problems with the traditional lithium battery voltage sampling circuit based on operational amplifier voltage conversion: First, the use of more high-voltage MOS transistor in the operational amplifier leads to the reduction of detection accuracy; Second, there is a current path from battery positive to the ground during voltage detection, and the detection current from the positive pole is also inconsistent. It leads to the imbalance of each battery after the end of the detection. This paper proposes a multi-cell battery-management-system voltage sampling circuit that uses the super source follower structure for battery positive voltage pretreatment and ordinary source follower for battery negative voltage pretreatment. The circuit ensures that the upper and lower voltage difference of the operational amplifier is within the low voltage range of a battery voltage and the input transistor gate-source voltage of the operational amplifier, which avoids the use of high-voltage MOS transisitor. At the same time, the detection current is provided by all series batteries, and there is no current outflow at the positive and negative, ensures balance of the battery. The simulation test is carried out under the conditions of 0.35umBCD process, ss, tt, ff process angle and temperature 27 °C, and the circuit function is normal. The positive and negative current of the battery is less than 1fA, and the voltage sampling max error is 1.4mV.

articleTitle: High voltage and high power IGBT performance optimization design
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Due to the complexity of the application requirements, the high-power IGBTs used in the power grid must possess not only a high breakdown voltage and a low saturation voltage, but also strong short-circuit robustness in the event of system failure, which poses a significant challenge in the industry design. In this paper, various IGBT buffer-layer concentration distribution profiles formed by different process combinations are studied. The key factor to optimized the relationship between IGBT static performance and short-circuit robustness is also explicated. By adjusting the combination of the buffer layers with different concentration distributions and P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> collectors with different concentrations, the design scheme of 4500V IGBT with superior performance and good short-circuit robustness is obtained.

articleTitle: Design of 40Gb/s PAM4 Signal SerDes Low Power CMOS 64:4 MUX
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper designs a low-power CMOS 64:4 MUX circuit for 40Gb/s PAM4 signal SerDes system. The circuit uses UMC28nm process with a 1.05V voltage. The circuit structure is composed of 4-stage cascaded 2:1 MUX and configurable clock module. Clock control sampling of 2:1 MUX per stage is used in a configurable clock scheme to guarantee maximum and provide clock drive. To reduce power consumption, 5Latch and 3Latch 2:1 MUX schemes are used. For different transmission rates, each stage 2:1 MUX using different structures to implement. Improving the robustness of the circuit, CMOS 64:4 MUX enables the conversion of 64-bit 625Mb/s parallel data into 4-bit 10Gb/s serial data under various PVT conditions. Abstract: This article designs a low-power CMOS 64:4 MUX circuit for the 40Gb/s PAM4 Signal SerDes system. The circuit adopts UMC28nm technology and a 1.05V power supply voltage. The circuit structure is composed of a 4-stage cascaded 2:1 MUX circuit and a configurable clock module. Using a configurable clock scheme, clock control sampling is performed on each stage of 2:1 MUX to ensure maximum timing margin and provide clock drive. In order to reduce power consumption, the 5Latch and 3Latch 2:1MUX scheme is adopted. For different transmission rates, 2:1MUX at each stage is implemented with different structures, which improves the robustness of the circuit. Under various PVT conditions, CMOS 64:4 MUX achieves the conversion of 64 bit 625Mb/s parallel data into 4 bit 10Gb/s serial data.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Digital Power Amplifier Design Based on 22-nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a digital power amplifier (DPA) with high power, high efficiency and six efficiency peak points is designed for polarized transmitter system based on 22-nm CMOS process. Power amplifier (PA) cells adopt the switched-capacitor PA (SCPA) structure. And the output port adopts a transformer-based four-in-one power combining network to achieve peak output power of more than 1 W. The power back-off (PBO) scheme using three efficiency-enhancement techniques, Class-G, Doherty and Time Interleaving (TI), produces six peak efficiency points. The simulated results show that the peak output power is 30.6 dBm at 2.4 GHz, and the drain efficiency are 52.7%, 51.1%, 52.0%, 46.6%, 39.6% and 23.5% at 0 dB, 2.5dB, 6 dB, 8.5 dB, 12 dB and 18 dB of power back-off. The DPA has the excellent amplitude modulation (AM)-AM distortion and the simulated AM-phase modulation (PM) distortion is less than 13°.

articleTitle: A Wide-Range and High-Linearity Timing Generator with 1.25ps-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a wide range and high resolution of the timing generator circuit is introduced. A high precision delay phase locked loop (DLL) technology is proposed, which uses two identical locking loops to offset the static phase error, realizes accurate delay locking and improves the circuit resolution. In the temperature range of −20 ~ 80°C, and the test clock signal ranges from 100KHz to 5GHz, the resolution is 1.25ps and covers a timing adjustment range of 10.4ns, with nonlinear INL less than 0.7 LSB and DNL less than 0.5 LSB.

articleTitle: Ultra low leakage planer back gate transistor realized by 12 inch RF PVD InGaZnO4 channel
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper reported a component controllable (In:Ga:Zn close to 1:1:1) high-purity indium gallium zinc oxide-InGaZnO4(IGZO) film deposition process through optimization of physical vapor deposition(PVD) process parameters(DC power, RF power, process pressure, O2 ratio) on a 12-inch room temperature RF magnetron sputtering platform. By adjusting the composition ratio of In, Ga, and Zn in the film, the carrier mobility, leakage of channel as electrical parameters inside the film can be balanced, a stable internal structure of the film can be obtained. To verify the process and performance of the obtained IGZO film, a component-stable IGZO film prepared by a 12-inch PVD process was used as the channel material to fabricate a planar bottom-gate transistor structure. The on-state current and off-state leakage current under different gate voltage scanning conditions were tested. Experimental data show that the transistor prepared under 4.5% oxygen partial pressure has an ultra-low leakage current of 10E-I2A and a switch current ratio of up to 10E7, the switch current ratio could be further optimized by integration method, such as gate oxide material and annealing in oxygen atmosphere. Such ultra-low leakage current transistors can be used in the field of dynamic random access memory (DRAM), forming a 2T0C structure of storage units with separate write and read paths. This not only allows non-destructive data storage reading but also significantly improves data retention time. Furthermore, because there is no traditional storage unit of capacitor structure, 3D stacking can be achieved, further improving the density of memory units per unit area.

articleTitle: Design of a 9-bit SAR ADC for Quad-channel VCSEL Transmitters
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 9-bit current-mode SAR ADC for automatic power control of quad-channel vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) optical transmitter is proposed in this paper. The ADC consists of an input selector, a current comparator, a 9-bit current-mode DAC, and clock generation and SAR logic control circuits. The good static characteristics of ADC are mainly implemented by using segmented DAC structure with low mismatch design, and the dynamic characteristics are mainly optimized by lowering the noise of SAR timing sequence. Designed in 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology, the ADC occupies an area of 0.05 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and consumes dynamic power of 2.9 mW under 1.8 V power supply. The simulation results show that the DNL and INL are within ±0.27 and ±0.26 LSB, respectively. At Nyquist frequency, its SFDR and ENOB are 50.87 dB and 7.29 bits, respectively.

articleTitle: An Improved Test Structure of Boundary Scan Designed for 2.5D Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: While chiplet provides more IC design opportunities, 2.5D advanced heterogeneous integration brings more challenges to test due to its complex structure and interconnection. This paper proposes an improved test structure of boundary scan aiming at the interconnection in different directions between 2.5D stacked chiplets. By segmenting the boundary scan chain inside each chiplet and make each segment configurable, we test interconnections in different directions between chiplets at the same time, with shorter test vector and smaller area compared to ieee 1149.1. Additionally, a new configuration method based on the standard TAP state machine is suggested in order to shorten the configuration time for interconnection testing. The total test vector in the scenario of three core interconnect testing is lowered by 76.58% compared to the standard one, additionally cutting the configuration time by 82.76% when compared to employing user-defined instructions reserved in the standard. The area is 10.65% smaller than the typical testing structure.

articleTitle: A 2.4-5.25GHz Active Feedback Balun-LNA With Variable Gain in 40nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A wideband active feedback variable-gain S-to-D LNA is proposed in this paper. It achieves low noise figure (NF) below 2 dB and a wide band gain of 28.7 dB in a band of 2.1 GHz~5.77 GHz. Current-reused CMOS structure and unbalanced CG-CS structure are applied to optimize noise performance under the power constraint condition and realize the conversion of signal from single to differential. The capacitive cross-coupling structure is used at output to suppress output imbalance. The differential output is connected to the voltage combiner and fed back to the input through a resistor to achieve wideband input matching. Based on TSMC 40 nm CMOS technology, the power consumption is below 20 mW at 1.2 V single supply. In high gain mode, voltage gain within 28.77 dB±0.5 dB is from 2.16 GHz to 8.54 GHz, NF below 2 dB from 1.4 GHz~6.65 GHz, IIP3≥-16.4 dBm and S11≤−10 dB. In low gain mode, across band of 2.4 GHz~5.25 GHz, voltage gain is about 0 dB, NF≤12.8 dB, ${\mathrm {IP}_{-1dB}}$ ≤ −5.84 dBm.

articleTitle: A 10/20/40/80 MHz 3rd-order Active-RC Butterworth LPF for 802.11ax Receiver
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable 10/20/40/80 MHz bandwidth Butterworth active-RC low-pass filter (LPF) in 55 nm CMOS for IEEE 802.11ax receiver is presented. This filter has a programmable in-band gain, which can save additional amplifier circuits and reduce analog baseband power consumption. Programmable capacitor array of the filter is used to adjust bandwidth. Adjust the gain ranging from 0 to 24 dB in-band by programmable resistor array. The prototype filter consumes a current 25.1 mA at 1.5 V supply and occupies 0.084 mm$^{2}$. The spurious free dynamic range (SFDR) of the LPF reaches 71 dB, and the NF is less than 35 dB over the filter’s bandwidth.

articleTitle: The Impact of CTLE Poles on Receiver Eye Diagrams
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As the data transmission demand increases, the time margin for receiver sampling becomes smaller rapidly. Particularly at the 224Gbps node, the overall time margin may be less than 1ps. Since the IUI-spaced feed-forward equalizer and decision-feedback equalizer cannot equalize the frequency responses above the Nyquist frequency in theory, the continuous-time linear equalizer becomes the only module in wireline receivers that increases the eye width. This paper constructs a bit-by-bit time-domain model of a receiver and discusses the relation between poles of continuous-time linear equalizer and the margin of the eye diagram. The simulation results show that when the channel noise is low, raising the poles can effectively increases the eye height and eye width. However, when the crosstalk noise is comparable to the amplitude margin, the eye opening will be overwhelmed if using poles higher than the Nyquist frequency.

articleTitle: Low Voltage and Low Power PLL with Current-Reuse Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a low voltage and low power charge pump PLL based on current-reuse LC oscillator is designed. Different from the traditional differential LC VCO, the VCO in this design uses the cross-coupled pair of PMOS and NMOS to achieve the effect of Current-Reuse. The phase noise of the VCO is not affected by the second harmonic term of the common source node. In order to further reduce power consumption, the design uses 0.8V low voltage power supply and all the MOSFETs adopt a low threshold structure. The simulation results show that the power consumption of the whole circuit is 1.2mW and the phase noise at 1MHz frequency offset is -109dBc/Hz when the PLL output is 1.8GHz under the TSMC 180nm process and 0.8V supply voltage. The whole PLL can achieve integer frequency division of 1.68GHz $\sim 1.92$ GHz, and the locking time is less than 10us.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband High Flatness Drive Amplifier Based on GaAs Process
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the RF front-end system, the drive amplifier require high flatness in the bandwidth. To adhere to the application requirements of the RF front-end circuit integration, miniaturization and high efficiency, based on the traditional theory of the drive amplifier and equalizer, this paper presents a design method to match the input impedance of the drive amplifier. This ensures that the matching network not only accommodates impedance matching but also enhances in-band flatness. To verify the reliability of this method, we developed a compact, high flatness drive amplifier utilizing the GaAs pHEMT process. The device operates in a frequency range of 2-6 GHz and covers WiFi, satellite and radio positioning. The small-signal gain is 23.5± 0.1dB, and both the input and output return loss are less than −12dB. Large-signal test reveal that the saturated output power of the whole broadband is greater than 22.5 dBm, and the corresponding power-added efficiency is greater than 34%. The test results demonstrate enhanced flatness compared to the traditional drive amplifiers.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Low-Noise Amplifier Combining Noise-Canceling and Self-Forward-BodyBias Techniques Achieving 2.9-to-3.7dB NF
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a single-ended to differential ultra-wideband (UWB) low-noise amplifier (LNA) is proposed, featuring the combination of noise-canceling (NC) and self-forward-body-bias (SFBB) techniques. By cross-connecting the NC networks, the noise due to the common-source and common-gate transistors at input can be effectively canceled. Besides, the SFBB technique is smartly introduced in the LNA to reduce the power supply and also for the power consumption. Furthermore, the current-reuse topology is employed for further reduce the power consumption. Implemented in 40nm CMOS process, our proposed LNA exhibits a gain (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) of 11.3 to 14.3dB with input-impedance matching (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) $\lt -10$dB for a frequency range of 3 to 5GHz. The noise figure (NF) is simulated $2.9 \sim 3.7$ dB, and the 3$^{rd}$order input-intercept point (IIP3) is -10.2 to -0.4dBm. Under 1V supply, the power consumption is 13mW. The active area is 0.25mm$^{2}$. The proposed LNA effectively achieves the purpose of low noise and low power consumption.

articleTitle: A 6-18 GHz Low Group Delay Variation Amplifier With Inductive ESD Protection for Phased-Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a ultra-wideband (UWB) amplifier with three cascaded stages to expand operational bandwidth. The shunt inductor at the input provides an electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection path to ground. Implemented in SMIC 40nm CMOS technology, the proposed topology achieves good input impedance matching, flat gain of 17.8–19.9dB and low group delay (GD) variations of 169.0 ± 61.4 ps over 6-18 GHz, simultaneously. The amplifier consumes 188.1 mW totally under a 2.5-V supply and the output 1 dB compression point $(\mathrm{O}\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{1dB}})$ is $\geq \mathrm{S} \mathrm{dBm}$. After elaborate optimization, the core chip occupies an area of $746\times 587\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$ excluding test pads and $883\times 724\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$ with pads included, respectively.

articleTitle: Front End Readout Circuit of a Novel Charge Sensitive Amplifier Based on Temperature Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A high gain and low noise front-end readout mix chip has been designed to address the temperature stability issue of the radiation detector front-end readout circuit. The chip integrates an analog to digital converter after each readout circuit channel, resulting in high overall signal processing efficiency. Improvements have been made to the key module charge sensitive amplifier circuit, proposing a multi-stage high temperature compensation charge sensitive amplifier circuit. This overcomes the temperature stability problem of using MOS transistors operating in the subthreshold region as feedback resistors, ensures that the amplifier maintains a basically constant discharge time over a wide temperature range, and ensures that the overall circuit has good temperature stability. A new type of peak detection hold circuit is used to eliminate the traditional RC delay unit and improve the stability and accuracy of the front end readout circuit. The simulation results show that the equivalent input noise charge of the front-end readout system chip is 29.52e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup>, gain is 200V/pC, power consumption is 5.52mW, the maximum nonlinear error is 7%.

articleTitle: A low-temperature drift current-mode relaxation oscillator with feed-forward period control
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A low-temperature drift current-mode relaxation oscillator circuit design using a feed-forward cycle control scheme is proposed. This design extracts the delay error from the circuit and compensates it to the charging process of the next cycle circuit. This design effectively solves the problem that the delay error is greatly affected by temperature and thus leads to excessive drift in the oscillation frequency. A relaxation oscillator circuit that can work at supply voltage from 3.2 V to 5 V is designed, The average temperature coefficient is 18.5 ppm/° C when the supply voltage is 3.3 V, and 14.3 ppm/° C when the supply voltage is 4.5 V in the temperature range of -40 °C to 120 °C, and its supply voltage coefficient is 0.27%/V from 3.2 V to 5.0 V. Notably, compared with the current-mode relaxation oscillator using the general design method, the temperature drift of the oscillator designed in this work is reduced by about 26% and 59% at 3.3 V and 4.5 V supply voltage, respectively, and the voltage drift is reduced by 75%.

articleTitle: A High-performance LCD Driver Analog Circuit Based on Charge Pump
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of unstable liquid crystal output caused by unstable traditional power supply voltage, an LCD driver circuit with high-performance charge pump is designed. Compared to a conventional charge pump circuit, the proposed charge pump circuit output voltage has no threshold voltage loss, and solves the problem of switch leakage by introducing a two-phase non-overlapping clock without increasing the circuit area. We realize a stable output voltage by adding an appropriate negative feedback module. A simulation with typical frequency of 24.0MHz is carry out in HHGrace 110nm CMOS process library and the measured output voltage of charge pump variation is ±0.02V for temperature changes from -40°C to 125°C with different process. The simulation results show that the charge pump output voltage does not change with the power supply voltage, and the output voltage of LCD has good accuracy at different temperature with different process corner, and does not change with the power supply voltage.

articleTitle: A 4% Impedance Variation JEDEC Compatible ZQ Calibrator for DDR3, DDR4 and DDR5 SDRAM
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper design and implement a common ZQ Calibration circuit, it can finish all calibration procedures within 60ns by 6 steps, and comparator is the important component in ZQ Calibrator, this paper utilizes a 10 kHz chopper to cancel the offset, and the offset is lower than 2mV after DCOC. this paper use multi voltage reference points for DDR3/DDR4/DDR5 calibration, DDR3 use 0.5*VDDQ as calibration point while DDR4/5 use 0.8*VDDQ. What’s more, DDR3 and DDR4 ZQ calibrator utilize external clock while DDR5 needs to use self-oscillator clock, so both external clock mode and internal clock mode are implemented in this paper, and the internal OSC period variation is lower than 10% by utilizing voltage and temperature compensation. Lastly, a scan test circuit is added in this design to facilitate ZQ calibrator test.

articleTitle: A Two-Step Reconfigurable Time-to-Digital Converter Based on Gate-Vernier Rings
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Time-to-digital converter (TDC) is currently a key technology in the fields of single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) time-resolved imaging. TDC has attracted widespread attention due to good resistance to the PVT variations and fine resolution. This paper presents a two-step reconfigurable TDC which is based on gate-vernier rings and self-biased phased-locked loop (SBPLL). The drawback of the Vernier ring oscillator is its long conversion time, So this paper proposes a reconfigurable vernier ring oscillator to meet the requirements of different dead times. The system adopts gating technique to reduce the power consumption. Designed in 180 nm CMOS standard process, the proposed TDC achieves 13.5-ps resolution, 40-ns dynamic range with 85-ns conversion time in the four-stage mode, and 26.9-ps resolution, 30ns conversion time in two-stage mode. The power consumption is 2.4 mW with 1.8 V supply voltage.

articleTitle: Architecture Analysis and Simulink Modeling of a High Resolution Zoom ADC
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper analyzes the principle of the architecture and key circuit modules of a high resolution discrete Zoom Analog-to-Digital Converter (Zoom ADC) used in multicolor detectors, and uses Matlab Simulink to model in the behavior level and verifies its function and performance. Zoom ADC uses a front-end coarse 5-bit Asynchronous Successive Approximation Register Analog-to-Digital Converter (SAR ADC) to dynamically adjust the reference voltage of a back-end fine third order 2-bit Sigma-Delta modulator (SDM) to effectively improve the dynamic range of the system. An additional feedforward path combined with a 2-bit quantizer minimizes quantization noise in SAR ADC, and the Data Weighted Average (DWA) algorithm performs first order noise shaping for capacitor mismatches in 5-bit fine Capacitance Digital-to-Analog Converter (CDAC),and introduces the over-ranging factor M, which not only relaxes the quantization error of SAR ADC, but also effectively prevents SDM overload. Simulink modeling results show that the signal to noise distortion ratio (SNDR) of the output signal is greater than 117 dB and the effective bit (ENOB) is greater than 19 bits when the input signal frequency is within the bandwidth of 10 KHz, the oversampling rate is 128, and the signal amplitude is −0.9dBFS.

articleTitle: A Case Study on the Internal Mutual Interference of Multitenant FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Previous researches have shown that a remote user can cause the circuit of another user in a cloud FPGA to fail by creating mutual interference inside the FPGA. However, the fundamental mechanism of mutual interference is still not clear. This paper conducts a series of tests to investigate the condition and the type of the function failure. Two critical parameters of the interference source, the number of interference units $({N}_{INT})$ and the frequency of the interference $({f}_{INT})$ are examined. The behavior of a microprocessor is monitored at the instruction level during the interference experiments. Our test results show that ${N}_{INT}$ is inversely proportional to ${f}_{INT}$ at the failure threshold. The relationship indicates that the deciding factor of interference source on the failure of the microprocessor is the average current. The ratio of interference frequency to microprocessor frequency plays no role in the failure threshold. It is observed that the malfunctions of the program count (PC) and the instructions are the main reasons for the system failure. The interference also causes the pipeline to stall. The results presented in this paper help to understand the bottom mechanism of FPGA failure under remote attack. It also helps to make countermeasures to protect the FPGA.

articleTitle: A 27.1 dB Gain and 6.85 dB NF Low-Noise Amplifier Based on the Novel Gain-Noise Plane
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a 160 GHz cascode low-noise amplifier (LNA) in $0.13 \mu \mathrm{m}$ SiGe BiCMOS with the gain-noise plane approach. The collaborative power gain and noise optimization is performed by analyzing the optimal region of the LNA and the character of the gain-state point on the gain-noise plane. Besides, the optimized stagger-tuned technology is derived theoretically to decrease the in-band noise performance degradation. The proposed cascode LNA achieves a power gain $(G_{p})$ of 27.1 dB, bandwidth of 31 GHz (148-179-GHz), noise figure (NF) of 6.85 dB, input-referred 1dB power compression point (IP1dB) of -23.9 dBm and power consumption of 31.6 mW.

articleTitle: A Strong-Arm Comparator Layout Design with Combined Expert Knowledge and Intelligent Optimization Algorithm in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Placement and routing are critical to the post-layout performance of analog circuits. This is primarily due to parasitic caused by device spacing during placement, wire length, and width during routing cannot be effectively controlled, regardless of whether the layout is generated manually or through the use of automation tools. In this work, a simple and effective layout design flow is proposed and implemented for the Strong-Arm comparator to improve its post-layout performance. To begin with, the Strong-Arm layout style adopted by expert designers is leveraged as the placement template. Subsequently, the critical variables impacting the arrangement of devices and the performance of the circuit such as spacing between key components and the width of critical nets are identified. Finally, these variables are sent to the intelligent optimization algorithm to adjust the layout till the post-layout results can closely match the schematic. Overall, by integrating expert knowledge and the intelligent optimization algorithm, our approach yields promising post-layout results for the Strong-Arm comparator. Under a 1-V power supply, the comparator exhibits a root-mean-square input-referred noise of 88.2uV, which deviates by only 2% from the noise of the schematic.

articleTitle: The Design of LTCC-based Miniaturized X-band T/R Module
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Active phased array radar is widely used in radar systems and electronic warfare. T/R module is one of the key components in the active phased array radar system. This paper takes advantage of high integration of LTCC technology to design an X-band four-channel miniaturized T/R module. This module adopts high-integrated technologies such as MCM and MMIC to integrate microwave circuits into multi-layer LTCC substrates. Finally, the designed and implemented T/R module has a volume of 46.35 mm $\times 59.2$ mm $\times 9.7$ mm, its transmit output power is greater than 46 dBm, its receive gain is better than 20 dB, and the noise figure is under 2.3 dB. This module has good performance and high engineering practical values.

articleTitle: A dB-Linear Variable Gain Amplifier for Zero-IF Receivers
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a variable gain amplifier (VGA) with a common mode feedback (CMFB) loop and DC offset cancellation (DCOC) for better application in the zero-IF receivers. The VGA chip is fabricated in a 22nm CMOS technology and consuming power of 2.8mW under the supply voltage of 1V. The VGA realizes the dB-linear gain dynamic range of 40dB and its curve between the gain and control voltage achieves the exponential relationship by cascading. The chip area of this VGA is $145 \times 100 \mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$. The 3dB bandwidth is up to 300MHz, significantly satisfying the operating frequency band of 50MHz. The OP1dB of this VGA is over 2dBm, ensuring the good linearity of the entire receiver.

articleTitle: A W-band Phase-Locked Loop with a Robust Injection-Locked Frequency Divider
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a W-band phase-locked loop (PLL) with a robust injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD). By using a frequency doubler, the voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) in the PLL loop operates at half the W-band frequency. The performance of the proposed ILFD is improved by incorporating an automatic injection bias adjustment mechanism that relies on a peak detector (PD) to sense the VCO’s output voltage amplitude. The injection transistors’ gate bias voltages are dynamically modified in accordance with the PD’s output. The proposed W-band PLL is designed in 28-nm CMOS technology with a core area of 0.11 mm$^{2}$. The simulated phase noise (PN) of the PLL is -94.6 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset with a carrier of 80 GHz. The frequency tuning range is 10% (76 GHz to 84 GHz), and the power consumption is 27 mW.

articleTitle: A 5.3-fJ/conv.-step Pipelined-SAR ADC with Resistance Assisted Two-Stage Dynamic Amplifier Based on Gm-Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This work presents a single-channel, fully dynamic SAR-assisted pipelined analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with a wide input range. The ADC employs a resistance assisted two-stage dynamic amplifier based on gm-unit to achieve outstanding residue amplification efficiency and settled-time. It has a small variation in input parasitic capacitance to achieve high linearity and leverages a bias compensation circuit to reduce the gain variation with a temperature drift. Moreover, an improved bootstrap switch with parasitic optimization, is adopted to achieve stable high sampling linearity over a large input frequency range. Based on the 28nm process, post simulation with noise shows that the ADC achieves a low-frequency SNDR of 67.4 dB and SFDR of 75 dBc at 500MS/s. Over Nyquist up to 900 MHz input, the SNDR and SFDR keep on 63.7dB and 67.6dBc. It consumes 5.1 mW from a 1V supply and occupies a area of 0.011 mm$^{2}$, leading to Schreier and Walden figure-of merit (FoM) values of 174.3 dB and 5.3 fJ/conv.-step, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Configurable I/O Expander with the Wide-range Voltage and Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: I/O expander is a popular device in embedded systems, often serving as system adhesive. It is commonly based on I2C to support bi-directional communication between multiple interconnected devices in a master-slave structure. After analyzing some products in the market, we have proposed a configurable I/O expander with the wide-range voltage and temperature. It consists of communication block, control block, interrupt block, and IO block. At the same time, we propose the ultra-low voltage design methodology to be compatible with as many devices as possible. In addition, we also insert BIST circuit to improve reliability and yield. After a series of simulation, the proposed design was fabricated in 0.35$\mu$m CMOS process, and the test on chip level is carried out after tape-out. The results show that the I/O expander has better performance and faster response compared with other works, which is very suitable for end-side devices in the IOT and servers.

articleTitle: A low power continuous time hysteresis comparator with an average current consumption of 614nA at 1.5 voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-power continuous time comparator with hysteresis for low speed and low power applications, such as duty cycle temperature sensors. A minimum current selector with hysteresis is proposed to reduce the bias current of the comparator when the differential input is large, and increase the bias current when the differential input is small, thereby converting the static bias current of the comparator into dynamic bias current to reduce power consumption. In addition, the increased hysteresis path makes the output of the comparator highly immune to disturbances. Furthermore, chopper is typically added to suppress 1/f noise and DC offset, and the comparator designed in this article combines chopper with hysteresis. The comparator is fabricated in 110nm CMOS technology, works under a 1.5V supply voltage, and has a average current of 530nA.

articleTitle: An 18.8-to-40.4 GHz reconfigurable multi-mode VCO with wide-band common-mode resonance
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an 18.8-40.4 GHz voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) for 5G FR2 band in 65-nm CMOS. This circuit uses two VCO cores to cover a wide tuning range. Each core is based on Class-B LC-VCO structure and equipped with 5-bit switched capacitors to extend its tuning range. The low Q wide-band common-mode resonance is used to optimize phase noise. The simulation results show that the proposed oscillator exhibits a 72.9% tuning range from 18.8 to 40.4 GHz and the phase noise performance is less than -105 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset. The figure of merit (FoM) is better than 186 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset in full frequency band.
