A state-of-the-art FoM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of 203.4-207.7 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset is achieved with power consumption of 4.63-6.86 mW. The variation range of FoM and FoM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> is 3.7 dBc/Hz over the full frequency range.

articleTitle: Impact of Proton Irradiation at Different Temperatures on 100 V VDMOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The impact of proton irradiation on 100 V N-channel VDMOSFETs at room temperature (RT) and low temperature (LT) (77K) was systematically investigated in this work. From our analysis, the degradation of the device’s electrical properties after proton irradiation was demonstrated. Particularly, at RT, the electrical properties recovered at the fluence of $1\times 10^{16}$p/c$\mathrm{m}^{2}$, which was attributed to the depositing energy of the incident protons inside the devices during irradiation, which caused continuous temperature rise, resulting thus in the annealing effect and facilitating the recovery of the device’s electrical performance. By comparing the acquired results during proton irradiation of the devices at RT and LT, it was revealed that the LT irradiation significantly affected the electrical properties of the devices. This effect indicates that LT promotes the irradiation-induced damage of the devices. For this reason, the impact of the temperature on irradiation damage should be considered in the radiation-hardened design.

articleTitle: The Design of Bidirectional Active Balun Chip Based on Power Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Balun is used to realize the mutual conversion function from single-ended to differential signal. Balun can be divided into passive structure and active structure. The passive balun has a large area when the operating frequency is below 1GHz, on the other hand, the Q value of on-chip inductance is low and on-chip balun can cause great loss, which seriously affect the miniaturization design of the system. Active balun can realize high integration design, but traditional one is only limited to one-way signal transformation. For bidirectional conversion, it requires the application of switches to control multiple signals and introduce additional insertion loss and noise. This paper presents a bidirectional active balun working in 60MHz, whose circuit adopts switching mode of power modulation to realize bidirectional conversion between single-ended and differential conversion. The simulation result shows the phase difference of two output signals generated by single-ended inputs and differential outputs is about 18° at a temperature range from −40°C to 85°C, with error less than 1°. The signals generated by differential inputs and single-ended outputs can achieve gain balance. Its combined gain S21 is 1.1dB, and has more than 65dB reverse port isolation and certain linearity. Therefore, the simulation result shows that the bidirectional active balun meets the application requirements, and also verifies the correctness of theoretical analysis. It can improve the chip integration in system application, and has a wide application prospect

articleTitle: A 1.5GS/s Single-Channel Pipelined ADC With Large Dither Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A 1.5GS/s12bit single-channel pipelined analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is presented in this paper. The ADC employs a novel large dither injection technique for non-linearity. At high sampling rates, the linearity of ADC is degraded due to the presence of ambiguous factors that result in harmonic distortion. By incorporating both charge dither and flash dither techniques, the proposed approach can exposure and correct nonlinear behavior without losing the dynamic range of ADC. The proposed technique is designed in a 2Snm CMOS technology. The results show an improvement in the spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) from 70.1dB to 73.4dB.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Fast Transient Digital-LDO with Adaptive Rising-Edge Logic Control
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: An ultra-fast transient response Digital Low Dropout Regulator (D-LDO) is proposed. The D-LDO incorporates adaptive rising-edge logic control and adaptive current allocation technique to enhance the transient response speed and overshoot. The proposed D-LDO is simulated in a 180nm CMOS process and achieves a quiescent current of $18.4 \mu \mathrm{A}$ when operated at input and output voltages of 1.2V and 1.1V. It achieves a maximum current efficiency of 99.0% and demonstrates a response time of $0.72 \mu \mathrm{s}$, with the undershoot and overshoot voltages at 103 mV and 63 mV, when subjected to load current switching between 1mA and 5mA.

articleTitle: A 8 Channels 14 bits 100 MHz Sample and Hold Circuit Based on Delay-Locked Loop Control
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to improve the sampling frequency and sampling accuracy of the analog-to-digital converter, a multichannel sample and hold circuit controlled by delay-locked loop was designed based on 40nm CMOS process. A low jitter and low power delay-locked loop with pseudo-differential delay unit was improved as the clock control input of the eight channels sample and hold circuit. In the case of not affecting the sampling precision of the sample and hold circuit, eight channels can be sampled in turn. The precision of the sample and hold circuit is 13.8 bits, the sampling frequency is 100 MHz, and the SFDR is 85 dB. The cascaded simulation of the circuit proved that the circuit can meet the precision requirements, and the structure has strong practicability.

articleTitle: An Automated Deployment with Reconfigurable Digital Controller for SRAM-based Computation-in-Memory
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on the computing mode of Compute-In-Memory, this article proposes a digital controller architecture for Compute-In-Memory. This architecture is based on a configurable on-chip network and a configurable kernel ARRAY, integrating mixed-signal with programmable near-memory digital computation, configurable buffering, and programmable control. The digital controller provides several fully parameterized operators that support network expansion. Control of the accelerator and end-to-end computation can be achieved by configuring the instruction register. Furthermore, this paper proposes an end-to-end neural network compiler that converts artificial neural network models in the Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) format into executable code instructions. Ultimately, these instructions will run on a heterogeneous embedded system composed of a microcontroller unit (MCU) and a computation-in-memory (CIM) accelerator. The instructions generated by the compiler fully leverage the configurable architecture to accomplish kernel mapping and dataflow scheduling, thereby significantly reducing the model deployment time. By accelerating the ResNet14 algorithm, the accelerator architecture can achieve a frame rate of 45 frames per second (FPS) and a peak throughput of 368.154 Giga operations per second (GOPS) at 10 MHz.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise Fast-Startup Low-Dropout Regulator with Off-Chip Filter Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a low-noise fast-startup low-dropout regulator with off-chip filter capacitor is presented, which is fabricated in a 180nm CMOS process. For achieving excellent output noise performance, two technique methods are adopted: reducing reference internal noise and applying off-chip filtering. In order to reduce the noise of the reference, a novel optimization method is proposed. At the same time, a fast-startup circuit is carefully designed to avoid off-chip filtering capacitor slowing down the startup time of the system. The integrated output noise of the LDO with an off-chip 47nF capacitor is 13.03$\mu V_{RMS}$, and the startup time is less than 41$\mu$s. The static current consumption is 45$\mu$ A@ 5V, and the chip occupies the area of 0.44mm$^{2}$.

articleTitle: A Continuous Blood Glucose Monitoring Front End IC Design with Large Input Range
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This work presents a method that allows continuous blood glucose monitoring and provides a complete circuit that can continuously process a larger range of input currents for the more sensitive needle electrodes with electrodeposition technology. The circuit uses switched-capacitor to differentially process the two parts of the signals from target electrode and background reference electrode, thus greatly reducing the interference current generated by the complex blood environment of the human body. This work also makes full use of the adjustable characteristics of the circuit by adjusting the frequency of sampling and capacitance size of the circuit for different input current ranges, which maintains the excellent performance of the circuit. The monitor and readout IC proposed in this paper reduces the overall power consumption to 0.98 mW under 3.3 V supply voltage, while it extends the input current range to more than $48 \mu \mathrm{A}$ with minimum input-referred noise of 16 pArms.

articleTitle: A-236.5dB Jitter-FoM Dual-Path RO-PLL With Improved Supply Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a compact Ring Oscillator (RO) based PLL with a dual-path architecture for small loop filter area and a RO design with Kvdd compensation to reduce 38dB supply sensitivity. The proposed dual-path PLL was implemented in 55nm CMOS. In post-layout simulation and MATALB, it achieves rms jitter of 0. S44ps with 3.1mW power, leading to a FoMjitter of −236.5dB while occupying 0.0084mm2 chip area.

articleTitle: A Compact Low-Loss Bi-directional Amplifier for Ku-band
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Conventional bi-directional amplifiers connect transceiver circuits through two T/R switches that are large in area and introduce some loss at high frequencies. In this paper, a compact low-loss bi-directional amplifier for Ku-band (receive: 12-13 GHz, transmit: 15.5-16.5 GHz) has been designed on a TSMC 65 nm 1P9M CMOS process and employs two triple-coil-coupled transceive matching network multiplexing transformers to connect transceiver circuits. When the circuit is in the transmitting state, the power amplifier achieves a 1 dB compression point of 6.321 dBm and the peak PAE is close 30%. When the circuit is in the receiving state, the low-noise amplifier boasts a remarkable in-band gain exceeding 25.7 dB, accompanied by a NF of less than 3.5 dB. The area of the triple-coil coupling transformer is approximately 200*200 $\mu \mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{2}}$, which reducing the overall area of the bi-directional amplifier. The high-frequency insertion loss of the structure is about 1 dB, which is less than the 2 dB insertion loss of conventional switches at high frequencies. This design can be widely used in Ku-band phased array radars.

articleTitle: A 2MHz, 97.4% Peak Efficiency, Heterogenous GaN/BCD 48-to-12 V Cascaded Switched Capacitor Converter With ZVS Auxiliary Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: It has been demonstrated that switched capacitor (SC) converters have the potential to achieve higher efficiency and higher power density than magnetic-based converter. With two conventiona12-to-1 SC converters cascaded, this article presents a 2MHz, 12-54V input intermediate bus converter (IBC) mainly to realize the typical use of 48-to-12 V (fixed 4:1 step-down ratio) for hybrid electrical vehicle and other modern advanced industry. Based on tridimensional heterogeneous integration (3D-HI) of gallium nitride (GaN) and bipolar-CMOS-double-diffused meta-loxide-semiconductor (DMOS) (BCD) technology, the novel driving strategy and zero voltage switching (ZVS) auxiliary technique suggested in this work, the proposed highly-integrated cascade SC converter sized $3.74\times 3.09$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> achieves one of the best overall metrics among the state of the arts. Verified through post-simulation, it features a peak efficiency of 97.4% and power density of 1.87 W/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Low Power PGA Design Based on the Switched Capacitor Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper designs a low-power programmable gain amplifier (PGA) applied to image sensor chips. The PGA adopts a switch capacitor array structure, which achieves programmable amplification between 1-4 times by changing the size of the input and feedback capacitors, which is used to process pixel output signals under different light intensities. The operational amplifier in PGA achieves a bandwidth of 13 M and a gain of 68dB at a bias current of $2\mu A$. Using a 55nm process and a 3.3V power supply voltage, the output voltage of the programmable gain amplifier with a variation of 200mV is established within 700ns, and its average power consumption is less than $3.63\mu W$. Under the application of the low-power design circuit proposed in this article, the average power consumption of the PGA module is reduced by about 72.14%.

articleTitle: Design of a low-pass filter for wideband transceiver
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a channel-select filter for wideband transceiver is designed using Gm-C structure. Schematic and layout of the design are completed in TSMC 0.13μm CMOS process. A transconductance amplifier used in Gm-C filter is investigated in depth. Considering the filter architecture, the transconductance amplifier are designed with source degeneration, common-mode feedback and common-mode feedforward. The transconductance amplifier is used to constitute Gm-C low-pass filter for completing the design of channel selection filter. According to post-layout simulation, the filter can be tuned among 156MHz, 102MHz and 79MHz. Power consumption of the filter is 3. 47mW. Total harmonic distortion is 0.5% at high frequency, 0.3% at medium frequency and 0.7% at low frequency. Stop-band attenuation at 2nd order harmonic is 28. 9dB, 27.2dB and 26. 5dB respectively. Input referred noise is smaller than 71nV/$\sqrt{\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z}}$.

articleTitle: Enhancing FPGA-Based YOLO Object Detection: Multi-Bank Storage Optimization and Model Refinement for Real-Time Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Object detection algorithms are widely used in image classification and detection tasks recently. Among the other algorithms, You Only Look Once (YOLO) performs better in real-time detection. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the algorithm require a large amount of computation and memory access. However, researchers tend to access parameters through the external memory in accelerator design, which leads to slow processing speed and high power consumption. Therefore, we propose a Multi-Bank storage structure that flexibly combines URAM and BRAM in storing feature maps, which significantly improves the throughput. We also improve the YOLOv3-Tiny model by distillation, quantization and pruning and make it more suitable for deployment in FPGAs. These methods can significantly reduce the number of parameters in the model while ensuring almost no decrease in detection accuracy. Finally, tested on VOC 2007, our model achieves a frame rate of 67.6 FPS with a reduction in mAP of 0.38%.

articleTitle: A 13-19GHz Broadband Phase Shifter Using 0.15µm GaAs pHEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a high-precision, wideband digital phase shifter structure designed for the 13GHz-19GHz frequency range. The proposed phase shifter consists of six units with a step size of 5.625°, a phase range of 0-360°, and 64 phase states. The phase shifter design includes bridge T-type topology for 5.625°, 11.25°, and 22.5° phase units, and a high-pass/low-pass grid topology for 45°, 90°, and 180° phase units. The phase shifter exhibits excellent phase shifting performance with input and output return losses of less than −13dB for the 64-state phase shifter. The insertion loss of the phase shifter is less than 8.1dB, while the root mean square error of the phase shifting is less than 2.8°, and the root mean square error of amplitude is less than 0.45dB. The digital phase shifter offers wide bandwidth and high phase accuracy, making it suitable for applications in microwave phased array T/R components, wireless communication, and other fields.

articleTitle: Equalization technology and Quantization analysis for Data-converter Based PAM4 SerDes Link
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper constructed the distribution function of input noise at the receiver side and quantization noise for 25 Gb/s data-converter based PAM4 (4-level Pulse Amplitude Modulation) serial link. In order to reflect realistic performance, the effect of both noise on the equalization performance were analyzed at first. Then, the FFE’s location and the tradeoff between quantization resolution of data converter and FFE tap were studied in detail. Simulation results show that Rx FFE architecture can outperform Tx FFE for a high Gaussian noise environment. And for Rx FFE architecture, more-tap DFE can effectively suppress quantization noise and make a great tradeoff with the quantization resolution of analog-to-digital converter (ADC), which can be suitable for a high-noise and low-quantization transmission link.

articleTitle: Slip Detection through Fusion of Visual-Tactile Data using Swin Transformer V2
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to enhance the stability of manipulator grasping tasks using a Swin Transformer V2 network model. The focus is on fusing GelSight Sensor single-mode vision, tactile data, and multi-modal information to improve the manipulator’s perception in complex environments. The Swin Transformer V2 model is introduced for its strong performance in image understanding. The paper explains how unimodal visual-tactile data are input to the network for feature extraction, followed by a fusion strategy to effectively combine different modalities. The proposed method is applied to a manipulator grasp-slide detection task, resulting in improved stability and accuracy by leveraging multi-modal perception of the environment. Experimental validation and comparisons demonstrate the superiority of the approach, showcasing its potential in enhancing grasping stability.

articleTitle: A Configurable Detector Based on Layered Belief Propagation for Massive MIMO Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detection plays a prominent role in the field of wireless communication. And with this trend, message passing detection (MPD) attracts a great attention since its advantages of high throughput and low complexity between distinct detection algorithms. Among various MPD algorithms, Gaussian approximate interference belief propagation (GAI-BP) detection can exhibit excellent convergence and performance in the different scenarios. However, its hardware design should be more efficient and flexible further. This paper proposes a novel semi-parallel hardware architecture for GAI-BP detection, aimed at improving its configurability using a layer scheduling scheme. Through this scheme, the proposed detector achieves a gain of 0.65 dB when compared to the original algorithm, while simultaneously accommodating multi-antenna radios through the proposed hardware design.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Harmony Search and Simulated Annealing Algorithm for Job Shop Scheduling Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to address the Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSSP) by combining the Harmony Search (HS) and Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm. The proposed method employs the SA algorithm to generate initial solutions and new solutions for the HS algorithm. By exploring a wide range of solutions including worse ones, SA can effectively navigate the complex search space and generate diverse solutions for HS to optimize. This results in enhanced global search abilities and improved convergence of the HS algorithm for JSSP. Experimental results demonstrate the efficiency and efficacy of the proposed approach in solving JSSP.

articleTitle: An LDO Current Limit Protection Circuit With Hiccup Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents an LDO current-limiting protection circuit with hiccup logic circuit, which solves the problem of continuous short-circuit current in the traditional LDO current-limiting protection when the LDO is shorted. The proposed current limiting protection circuit can detect the output current and output voltage of LDO. And the current-limiting protection circuit will periodically detect whether the LDO is still in a short-circuit state. When the LDO is shorted, the current-limiting protection circuit will periodically cut off the LDO feedback loop, so that the output current only exists for a period of time. The simulation results show that the maximum output short-circuit current is 65mA, and the hiccup mode can save up to 85% of the short-circuit power consumption, which proves that the short-circuit hiccup mode has obvious effects and effectively prevents the chip from overheating. This current limiting protection circuit can be applied to various LDO current limiting protection circuits.

articleTitle: A 0.075mm² Octave-Tuning 5G-NR Oscillator with E-M Mixed-Coupling Achieving 205dB FoMT
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This article proposes a dual-core quad-mode millimeter-wave voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO), featuring orthogonal-coupled transformers with E-M mixed-coupling topology. The proposed VCO can simultaneously achieve low phase noise and octave frequency tuning range using four reconfigurable resonant frequencies. In order to expand the tuning range of the electrically coupled capacitors, we propose a capacitive cross-connection method of the electric field coupling. Furthermore, unlike the traditional fixed coupling factor of the parallel 8-shaped transformer, our proposed orthogonal-coupled transformer can easily adjust the coupling factor by changing the distance between coils. Implemented in 65nm CMOS process, the oscillator has a 66% tuning range in the frequency range of 19.4 to 3S.5 GHz. At a 1 MHz offset, the VCO achieves a simulated phase noise below −104.6dBc/Hz and a FoM above 186.5 dBc/Hz over the whole frequency range. The chip consumes 4.9-9.7mW and an active area is 0.075 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A 0.4-2 GHz Wideband LNA Exploiting Noise Reduction and High Gain
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband low-noise amplifier (LNA) with noise reduction and high gain technology is proposed. The series peaking approach is used in this wideband LNA design to enhance the high frequency gain response, and a two-stage amplifier further widens the bandwidth (BW). The technology further makes use of current reuse and boosts transconductance of the CS transistor while maintaining low power consumption. Simulated in $0.25 \mu \mathrm{m}$ InGaAs pHEMT process, the proposed LNA is capable of driving an external 50$\Omega$ load and achieves noise figure (NF) of 0.92-0.96 dB and input return loss (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) better than -12 dB over the whole bandwidth. The LNA achieves high gain (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) of 30 dB and 1 dB com-pression point (OP1dB) of 16 dBm, respectively.

articleTitle: High-performance Ga2O3 Schottky Barrier Diode with a Self-aligned Shallow Groove and Dual Field-plate
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A novel $\beta$-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> Schottky barrier diode (SBD) with a self-aligned shallow groove (SG) and dual field-plate is proposed. The peak electric field around anode is suppressed by the self-aligned SG and dual field-plate. Compared with a conventional SBD, the breakdown voltage $(V_{br})$ of the novel device increases from 400V to 2200V, and the specific on-resistance $(R_{0\text{n},\text{sp}})$ increases from $4.1\text{m}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^{2}$ to $4.4\text{m}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}^{2}$. The power figure of merit $(V_{\text{br}}^{2}/R_{\text{on}\cdot\text{sp}})$ is $1.1\text{GW}/\text{cm}^{2}$. The variable temperature IV test shows that the prepared device has good temperature characteristics. These results suggest that a self-aligned SG and dual field-plate, composite terminal structure is an effective method with which to improve the performance of a $\beta$-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>.

articleTitle: A Sub-1.4 dB Noise Figure 6-18 GHz Low Noise Amplifier Using 0.15 µm GaAs pHEMT Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a 6-18GHz ultrawideband low noise amplifier (LNA) based on 0.15 µm GaAs pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistor (pHEMT) technology. The LNA generates flat gain, low noise figure, and acceptable input and output return losses from 6-18 GHz using a cascode structure, source degenerate inductors, and RLC negative feedback networks. Simulation results show that the noise figure is lower than 1. 4dB, the gain of the LNA is 24.5±1dB, and both input and output return losses are less than −10dB. The input 1dB compression point (IPldB) of the LNA is −10dBm.

articleTitle: A 4.0-μVrms 7.5-kHz-BW Neural Signal Recording Circuit for Closed-Loop Deep Brain Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This work presents a low-noise biosignal acquisition application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) for neural signal recording in closed-loop deep brain stimulation (DBS). An ac-coupled low-noise amplifier (LNA) amplifies the signals of interest while removing the low-frequency electrode offset. An improved programmable-gain amplifier (PGA) employs a flip-over-capacitor structure to prevent the degeneration of frequency response from switches’ off-state resistance. The differential-difference amplifier (DDA) used in the PGA isolates the switching noise from the following switched-capacitor low-pass filter that defines the upper limit of the bandwidth. A 12-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) converts the signals to digital representations with a sampling rate of 21.5 kS/s. The proposed circuit was fabricated in a 180 nm CMOS process with an area of 0.576 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, consuming 60 μA under a 1.8-V supply. It achieves a programmable gain from 47.3 dB to 59.1 dB. The measured input-referred noise is 1.74 μV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</inf> (1 Hz–300 Hz) and 3.73 μV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</inf> (300 Hz–7.5 kHz). The ADC used for digitization achieves an ENOB of 10.63 bits.

articleTitle: Transformer Design for Transformer- Coupled Multi-phase Voltage-controlled Oscillators (VCOs)
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This This paper presents transformer design for voltage-controlled oscillators (VCOs). It first presents a quadrature voltage-controlled oscillator (QVCO), which consists of four symmetric complementary cross-coupled sub-VCOs coupled by a loop inductor through magnetic coupling. The circuit design uses the concept of traveling wave and standing wave oscillators. The first proposed CMOS QVCO has been implemented with the TSMC 0.18μu 1P6M technology and the die area is $1.2 \times 1.2$mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. At the supply voltage of 1.3 V, the total power consumption is 23.66 mW. The free-running oscillation frequency of the QVCO is tuneable from 3.67 to 4.25 GHz GHz as the tuning voltage is varied from 0.0V to 2.5V. The measured phase noise at 1MHz frequency offset is −125.34 dBc/Hz at the oscillation frequency of 3.67 GHz and the figure of merit (FOM) of the proposed QVCO is -182.89 dBc/Hz. The second QVCO uses 2.5:2.5 transformer.

articleTitle: Lamé-Mode Resonator with Trapezoidal Grooves Based on Sc0.3Al0.7 N/AlN Composite Film Achieving Coupling Coefficient of 18.7%
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This work proposes a novel Lamé-mode resonator with trapezoidal grooves, using a 30% scandium-doped aluminum nitride ($\mathrm{Sc}_{0.3}\mathrm{Al}_{0.7}\mathrm{~N}$) and aluminum nitride (AIN) composite film ($\left.\mathrm{Sc}_{0.3}\mathrm{Al}_{0.7}\mathrm{~N}/\mathrm{AlN}\right)$ as the piezoelectric layer (cTGLMR). The slope angle of trapezoidal grooves is 80°. With the increase of groove depth, electromechanical coupling coefficient $(k_{eff}^{2})$ achieves the maximum value of 18.7% and figure of merit $(FoM$) reaches up to 150 when the groove depth is $0.6\mu\mathrm{m}$. The impact of design parameters on these resonators are systematically investigated by using finite element analysis (FEA). This structure shows broad application prospect for wide bandwidth filters.

articleTitle: A BW-Extended Blocker-Tolerant Receiver with RF Passive-Gain and High-Order BB Impedance Achieving 30dBm OOB-IIP3 and 110MHz RF-BW
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A bandwidth (BW)-extended blocker-tolerant receiver (RX) is proposed, which is characterized by a high-linearity fully-passive differential RF front-end and an enhanced RF selectivity $2^{\text{nd}}$-order baseband (BB) impedance. In order to relaxing the trade-off between the linearity and noise figure (NF), the implicit capacitive stacking technique is employed at radio frequency (RF) front-end to provide 6dB passive gain. Meanwhile, the complex poles introduced in $2^{\text{nd}}$-order $BB$ impedance are aimed to simultaneously achieve 40dB/ decade roll-off and widen RF-BW. When implemented in 65nm CMOS process, the simulation results show that at $\Delta\mathrm{f}=4X RF-BW$ the $RX$ achieves 30 dBm OOB-IIP3 and 110 MHz channel BW. Covering from 0.4 to 2.5 GHz, the NF ranges 4.2 to 5.5dB while the RX consumes a reasonable power of 26.8 to 77.2mW.

articleTitle: A FPGA-based high efficiency and low-power system for blood pressure measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this work, a high efficiency and low-power system for blood pressure(BP) measurement has been designed. The system integrates the algorithm of BP calculation using hardware description language. Therefore, there is no need to keep flash to store the program any more, nor is the MCU core. As a result, the core size could be very small. To realize the goal of ultra-low power, we adopt clock gating technique and an unconventional ADC for the sampling and converting of the pressure signal. The system is implemented with a Xilinx board and tested among 300 peoples. The results show that the mean absolute error of both systolic and diastolic blood pressure is less than 3mmHg.

articleTitle: A 10-bit 100-MS/s 1.2-mW Asynchronous SAR ADC with Low-power Dynamic Logic Units in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents a 10-bit 100-MS/s 1.2-mW asynchronous SAR ADC with low-power dynamic logic units in a 65nm CMOS process. To reduce power consumption, a dynamic logic cell capable of being turned off is proposed. Furthermore, a bootstrap switch is introduced to enhance linearity. The use of MIM capacitors ensures more accurate capacitance values. The ADC achieves both speed and accuracy objectives without the need for digital calibration in the background. Notably, it exhibits remarkable power efficiency. The prototype SAR ADC fabricated in 65nm CMOS achieves 40.07 dB SNR and 39.88 dB SNDR with low-frequency input while consuming only 1.2mW in total.

articleTitle: GPU Accelerated Harmonic-Balance Small Signal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Harmonic-balance (HB) small signal analysis is an important feature in RF circuit simulation. In this paper, we evaluate computational bottlenecks of HB small signal analysis on a CPU platform, especially for post-layout circuits at advanced process nodes. We then present an algorithm in dealing with HB small signal analysis on a graph processing unit. We developed a method that fully exploit the coherent parallelism of frequency sweeping, such that simulation efficiency is significantly improved. Our results show that the computational efficiency has increased by an order of magnitude on the graph processing unit comparing with that on the CPU platform.

articleTitle: A High-PSRR and Curvature-Compensated Subthreshold Voltage Reference Without Special Devices or Resistors
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, a high power supply rejection ratio (PSRR) and curvature-compensated subthreshold voltage reference free of special devices and resistors is presented. The proposed voltage reference (VR) exhibits four excellent properties: high PSRR, low temperature coefficient (TC), reduced power consumption and compact layout area. By utilizing cascode current mirror, a decorrelating transistor, a low pass filter and a three-branch structure, both low and high frequencies present high PSRR. In order to reduce the TC of the VR, a proportional to absolute temperature (PTAT) current obtained from an inverse diode is added to an active load, thus achieving curvature compensation. Furthermore, the VR consists solely of MOSFETs, most of which operate in subthreshold region, so the VR occupies a very small area and consumes fairly low power. The proposed VR is designed in a standard TSMC 180 nm process and occupies 0.032 mm$^{2}$ active area. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed VR operates desirably over a supply range of 1 V to 3.5 V with a line sensitivity of 0.047 %/V. The TC is 18.4 ppm$/^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ with a temperature range of -$30 \sim 120$ only consuming a quiescent current around 46 nA, and the PSRR approximates -80 dB at 100 Hz, and -45 dB at 1 GHz owing to special circuit structures.

articleTitle: 50Gb/s high-speed serial interface receiver CTLE equalization circuit design
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In high-speed interface circuits, a continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) is typically used at the receiving end to eliminate the effect of intersymbol interference (ISI) on signal transmission. In order to improve the shortcomings of traditional CTLE, such as limited single-stage compensation ability and excessive layout area caused by the use of large capacitors, a two-stage CTLE circuit is designed. The first stage CTLE adopts a transconductance cascade transimpedance (TAS-TIS) structure, consisting of two parts: a high-pass transconductance amplification (Gm-HF) circuit and a transimpedance amplifier (TIA) circuit. The GM-HF circuit uses active inductance as load and source-level negative feedback network and other technologies, which can effectively expand the operating frequency of the circuit without adding additional power consumption, while saving the area of the layout. The TIA circuit uses a transimpedance amplifier structure based on an inverter unit, which uses voltage-current feedback to reduce the input resistance value and increase the input bandwidth of the signal. The second stage CTLE adds a feed-forward path between the input transistor and the inductor, thereby increasing the gain lift of the circuit without affecting the gain of the low frequency. The simulation results show that the eye diagram eye width of the 40Gbps PAM4 (four-level pulse amplitude modulation) signal, 50Gbps PAM4 signal and 28Gbps NRZ (non-return-to-zero code) signal after equalization reaches 0.68/0.5/0.92 code element intervals (UI), respectively, and the eye height reaches 280/200/690 mV.

articleTitle: FeOCl monolayer as a promising anode material for alkali metal batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper utilized first-principles calculations to investigate the potential of FeOCl monolayer as an anode material for alkali metal batteries, specifically Li, Na, and K batteries. The focus of the research was on the adsorption and diffusion of alkali metal atoms on the FeOCl monolayer. The results showed that the FeOCl monolayer exhibited excellent adsorption of Li, Na, and K atoms with absorption energies of 3.4, −2.5, and −2.2 eV, respectively, surpassing traditional graphene’s adsorption (−1.673eV). The charge transfer from Li, Na, and K to the FeOCl monolayer was also predicted, and the FeOCl monolayer demonstrated good electronic conductivity and retained its metalloid properties. The diffusion potentials of Li, Na, and K on the FeOCl monolayer were found to be 0.15 eV, 0.12 eV, and 0.08eV, respectively. The largest storage capacities for Li, Na, and K on the FeOCl monolayer were 626.1, 500.9, and 267.4 mAh/g, respectively. Additionally, the open circuit voltage of FeOCl was measured to be 0.75 V for Li, 0.56 V for Na, and 0. S3V for K, indicating that FeOCl can provide a higher output voltage. Overall, the FeOCl monolayer holds potential as an anode material for Li-ion, Na-ion, and K-ion batteries.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Active Phased Array Beam Steering System Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: With its precise and adaptable scanning technique, phased array radar has been extensively used in both military and civilian applications since its introduction. Phased array radar technology is simultaneously evolving toward technology, shrinking, and integration. The beam control unit, which is unquestionably a major component, surely has the same development trend. The development of the wave control code algorithm and hardware circuit design for a centralized wave control system based on the FPGA Cordic algorithm are presented in this work. Currently, the FPGA control board is used for the hardware board-level verification test, and error analysis is done by comparing the hardware verification results with Matlab computation results.

articleTitle: An Adaptive All-Digital Phase-Locked Loop Architecture for High-Stability MEMS Temperature-Compensated Clocks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Silicon-based Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) clocks suffer from temperature drift, which severely affects the stability of their output frequency. In order to obtain a high-precision and stable clock frequency, a temperature-compensated all-digital phase-locked loop (ADPLL) based on a counter structure is proposed in this paper. The system dynamically adjusts the frequency control word according to temperature changes, enabling the unstable signal with frequency deviation to be locked at 25MHz, achieving the goal of temperature compensation and realizing a high-stability silicon-based MEMS TCXO (temperature-compensated crystal oscillator) clock. The proposed ADPLL includes five customized or semi-customized digital modules: reference phase accumulator (RPA), variable phase counter (VPC), time-to-digital converter (TDC), infinite impulse response (IIR), and phase error calculator (PEC). The TDC uses a programmable divider for frequency synthesis, only performing digital quantization in the phase detection part. The output is generated by a digital control oscillator (DCO) based on the phase error. In this paper, the issue of insufficient stability of silicon-based MEMS clocks is first introduced, followed by a detailed description of the specific design of the ADPLL-based adaptive temperature compensation system. Finally, the paper presents the behavior-level modeling design of the ADPLL and the FPGA simulation.

articleTitle: Failure Analysis of Abnormal Input Voltage in Error AMP Part of the PWM Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper explains the process of failure localization and mechanism analysis for a pulse width modulator failure case. The input voltage of the error amplification part of the pulse width modulator is zero. The input terminal has low resistance to ground. The failure phenomenon is unstable. It will change with changes in temperature, vibration, and other factors. Under certain conditions, the failure can recur. The analysis adopts a series of analysis ideas such as non-destructive troubleshooting, internal positioning, and replication verification. The collapse and deformation of the input bonding wires is an internal failure phenomenon of the PWM Controller. It connects the metallized edges of the chip. The metallization in this area is not covered by the passivation layer. This leads to a short circuit between the input and ground. The thermal expansion and contraction of the collapsed bonding wires during temperature cycling can lead to the unstable failure. And the movement of the bonding wires position during vibration can also lead to the unstable failure. This paper summarizes the research ideas and results. Especially the continuous and repeated adjustment of ideas can provide a reference for the subsequent failure analysis of similar and unstable failure.

articleTitle: A Path-Based System-Level Placement and Routing Framework for Muti-FPGA Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Multi-FPGA systems (MFSs) are widely used in the field of circuit prototyping and verification due to their excellent performance and scalability. In the compilation process of multi-FPGA systems, the solution to the minimum cut is often emphasized, but it is not an accurate objective for optimizing system performance. However, optimizing the final timing poses certain challenges. In this paper, a Path-based system-level placement and routing method is proposed to optimize the system performance. The algorithm utilizes the paths in the netlist to guide the placement and routing of the FPGA. It also utilizes the hardware resource utilization to guide the timing updates of the system, reducing the frequency of computing system timing. The experimental results demonstrate a 27% improvement in the maximum path delay with our proposed algorithm compared to the algorithm that does not consider path information.

articleTitle: MEMS-Enabled Computational Spectrometer Using A Denoising Autoencoder for Enhanced Reconstruction Resolution
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: On-chip spectrometers using silicon photonics offer a practical and economical solution for wearable electronics and portable instruments. However, noise affects the resolution of spectral reconstruction. Here, we propose and demonstrate an on-chip computational spectrometer combining MEMS time-domain modulation of a reconfigurable waveguide coupler and a denoising autoencoder. According to the noise-free assumption, the spectral reconstruction resolution is 0.3 nm. A convolutional autoencoder is designed to reduce noise and minimize its impact on the reconstruction resolution. At a noise level of 30 dB, the reconstruction resolution within a 100 nm bandwidth is improved from 1.1 nm to 0.4 nm, which is close to the 0.3 nm resolution of the condition without noise.

articleTitle: A 0.008mm2 -65dB PSR Analog-Digital Hybrid Capless LDO Using Switched-Capacitor Resistors and Frequency Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an analog-digital hybrid capless low-dropout voltage regulator (LDO). The analog-digital hybrid architecture gives a good balance between power consumption and performance. The area of the proposed LDO is dramatically reduced by using switched-capacitor resistors (SCR) as the feedback resistors, based on the internal clock to generate positive feedback, accelerate the system to recovery stability, and the load transient response performance is improved by adopting an auxiliary transient compensation loop. The proposed capless LDO achieves a small area of 0.008mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and a high PSR of −65 dB. In addition, it achieves 2mV/V line regulation, with an input voltage range of 2.9V to 3.5V. This design has a low quiescent current consumption of 5.7$\mu$A and a maximum output current load capability of l0mA. This design is implemented in SMIC 0.18$-\mu$m standard CMOS process.

articleTitle: 10GS/s 10bit Time-interleaved SAR ADC in 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a I0GS/s10-bit 32-way time-interleaved (TI) successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) in 28nm CMOS. The ADC core consists of four slices, with one sample front end shared by eight SAR ADC in each slice. A CMOS clock distribution, a high-speed front end and digital calibration of time skew and offset error are combined to optimize the ADC’s performance. Simulation results show that the calibrated SAR ADC reaches 52.8 dB SNDR and 60.2 dB SFDR at Nyquist input. The ADC power dissipation is 157 mW, corresponding to an FoM of 44 fj/con.

articleTitle: Soft-Start with Hiccup Mode Short-Circuit Protection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Aiming at the voltage overshoot and output short-circuit problems of DC_DC switching power supply, a soft start circuit with hiccup mode short circuit protection is designed. Soft-start eliminates voltage overshoot caused by power-on, while short-circuit hiccup protection makes the system work safely and effectively. The structure proposed in this paper additionally realizes the short-circuit protection with “hiccup mode” in the traditional soft-start circuit, which saves the layout area. In addition, the circuit uses MOS capacitors instead of traditional MIM capacitors to further reduce the soft-start layout area. A DC_DC switching power supply chip is designed using 0.4 um BCD process to verify the proposed soft start circuit. The simulation results show that the power chip successfully realizes the soft start and short circuit protection mechanism. The layout area of the soft start is only 0.122 mm × 0.109 mm, and the power consumption is about 0.00612 mW.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Miniaturized Filter Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In order to meet the application requirements of RF front-end circuit integration, miniaturization and high efficiency, compared with the traditional concept of direct cascading of power amplifier and filter, this paper proposes a design method of co-designing high out-of-band rejection filter and power amplifier matching network, which matches the input impedance of the filter directly to the optimal output impedance of the drain of the output stage of the power amplifier, so that the filter network has both filtering and impedance transformation functions. By matching the input impedance of the filter directly to the optimal output impedance of the drain of the power amplifier output stage, the filter network here not only has the function of filtering but also has the function of impedance transformation. In order to verify the effectiveness and practicality of the method, a broadband miniaturized filtered power amplifier with integrated filtering characteristics is designed to operate in the 14-18 GHz satellite communication band by taking advantage of the high output power of GaAs pHEMT devices. Simulation results show that, under the premise of maximizing the output power and efficiency of the power amplifier, the gain is up to 23 dB, the input and output returns are below -15 dB, the minimum power added efficiency is 46%, the suppression of out-of-band signals reaches -30 dB, and the power suppression of the high harmonics reaches -50 dBc, which is a great improvement compared with the out-of-band suppression of conventional power amplifiers.

articleTitle: Efficient Configurable Modular Multiplier For RNS
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Modular multipliers are usually the most critical units in Residue Number System implementations. With the widespread application of cryptographic algorithms based on the Residue Number System, the scale and variety of modulus channels have significantly increased, Consequently, the design of high-speed general-purpose modular multipliers has become increasingly important. In this paper, we propose a universal architecture for designing an efficient modular multiplier based on the Barrett reduction algorithm. The proposed modular multiplier can be configured to support different modular multiplications and is well-suited for accelerating applications in Residue Number System-based encryption schemes. Synthesized results demonstrate that the proposed modular multiplier exhibits up to a 35.7% improvement in performance compared to the improved Barrett modular multiplier.

articleTitle: DC and RF Small Signal Modeling of 28nm Planar MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In this paper, DC model and RF small signal model of 28nm planar MOSFET are proposed respectively. First, using the industry standard model, the Berkeley Short-Channel IGFET Model (BSIM), a DC global model of the MOSFET is established. An RF small-signal model up to 100 GHz is also obtained accurately. A nonlinear rational function is fitted to obtain the parameters. Due to the physical limitations of the mathematical model, the RF small-signal model is fitted with the RF quality factor. The analysis of the parasitic parameter variations at different voltages is performed. Good agreement is obtained between the equivalent circuit-modeled and TCAD-simulated data, which verifies the reliability of the model.

articleTitle: A wide input low quiescent current without operational amplifier bandgap reference circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The output voltage of traditional first-order temperature-compensated bandgap reference (BGR) fluctuates widely with temperature, which resulting in inaccurate supply voltages. This paper presents an improved high-performance bandgap voltage reference with wide input voltage range and low quiescent current. The circuit adopts a negative feedback loop instead of an operational amplifier, thereby reducing the influence caused by the operational amplifier. A wide range input (4~35 V) is achieved with a pre-bias circuit and the curvature compensation is realized by using the negative temperature characteristics of the triode and the characteristics of the MOS transistor working in the linear region The proposed BGR is implemented in a 0.18 ${\mu}$ m BCD CMOS process. The simulation results show that the designed bandgap reference has an output voltage of 1.205 V with the temperature coefficient of $3.83 \times 10 -6/^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ over the temperature range of −55°C to 125°C, and it achieves the PSRR of about −96 dB in the low frequency band with a current consumption of only 23 $\mu$A at 4.4 V power supply.

articleTitle: A New Strategy to Recover Threshold Voltage of SiC MOSFET After Gamma Radiation by Self-Heating in Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper provides a new strategy to recover the threshold voltage of SIC MOSFET after gamma radiation by self-heating in circuit, where the half-bridge topology is adopted. The safe self-heating of the SIC MOSFET can be realized by operating at the short circuit mode with a low current. The circuit board for self-heating of SiC MOSFET is designed. An appropriate control setting is found by experiments. After one time of 2 ms safe self-heating with power consumption from 65 W to 360 W, the threshold voltage of SIC MOSFET after gamma radiation is found to be recovered by 0.23 V∼0.42 V, which is about 29%∼47% of threshold voltage reduction (0.78 V∼0.9 V) by gamma radiation. In addition, more times of safe self-heating can further recover the threshold voltage by 27% (i.e., 0.23 V).

articleTitle: A 4th Order Chebychev Active-RC Low-Pass Filter With 5/10/20/30/40/50 MHz Tunable Bandwidth and Low Power
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on 40nm CMOS process, a tunable fourth order Chebychev low pass filter design was proposed for analog baseband circuits. The filter consists of two cascaded Tow-Thomas biquads and a clock-controlled series peripheral interface. The Tow-Thomas biquads utilized feedforward-compensated operational amplifiers. Tunable Capacitors and resistors were introduced to adjust the bandwidth. Simulation results show that the filter achieves a bandwidth of 5/10/20/30/40/50MHz with in-band fluctuations no more than 0.4 dB and its input-referred third order intermodulation point is at 15.6 dBm. The power consumption of the whole circuit is less than 5 mW. The filter layout occupies 751$\times 551 \mu m ^{2}$.

articleTitle: Investigation of a High Power Density Vertical IGBT with Zero Tail Current
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Based on the method of hole-carrier movement control and structure of the controllable trench gate (CTG) in the literatures, we propose a novel NPT IGBT with partial N buffer structure. In cooperation with the CTG, the partial N buffer realizes uniform potential distribution in drift region at the blocking state; introduces the dual-carrier split current conduction mode; and bypasses the electron carriers at the transition state. As a result, the breakdown voltage (BV) and on-state current density of the hole-controlled IGBT (HC-IGBT) 1.5 and 2 times than that of the conventional FS-IGBT. As a NPT IGBT with hole-carrier control, the HC-IGBT realizes zero tail current at the switching state at the bus voltage and current density of 600V and 600 A/cm$^{2}$, respectively, the switching loss of which, is 2 orders of magnitude smaller than its FS-IGBT counterpart according to the simulation results.

articleTitle: Workable Use of AlGaN/GaN D-Mode MIS-HEMTs in Realization of Highly Linear Passive Mixers Without Negative Biasing
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: On-wafer measurements were performed for AlGaN/GaN metal-insulator-semiconductor high electron mobility transistors (MIS-HEMTs) configured as single-ended radio-frequency (RF) mixers. While the depletion-mode (D-mode) HEMTs have a negative threshold voltage, the RF passive mixer design requires no negative biasing and draws no electrical power. A conversion loss as small as 13 dB is obtained, which is quite close to the ideal value of 9.9 dB for a single-ended passive mixer using a perfect switch. The 1-dB compression point (at the input) ranges from −1.3dBm to 5 dBm for different aspect ratios of the MIS-HEMTs. With a local oscillator (LO) power of 1 dBm, an input third order intercept point (IP3) of 12 dBm is obtained for a MIS-HEMT of W/L = 100/3, achieving a linear efficiency of 11 dB. The experimental results demonstrate the workable use of D-mode MIS-HEMTs as they are in realizing RF mixers for development of RFICs on gallium nitride (GaN) technology. With adjusted design, the normally-on device property of the MIS-HEMTs does not deter their direct use in proper circuit construction.

articleTitle: A High-power Microwave Switch Design
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Microwave switches are an important component of microwave control circuits, widely used in radar, satellite, communication, electrical countermeasures, and measurement. Their main function is to control the on-off of signals or complete the switching of signals between different channels. This article uses microwave PIN switching diodes to design a high-power microwave SPDT (Single-Pole-Double-Throw) switch for achieving microwave signal switching function.

articleTitle: Complete Timing Model of ECSM Lookup Table for CMOS Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: In the early days, engineers used non-linear delay models (NLDM) to estimate the circuit delay information. However, the accuracy of NLDM lookup table (LUT) decreases with the continuous change of the process, which makes the delay estimation become a difficult problem. Therefore, the effective current source model (ECSM) is proposed. The ECSM is a LUT composed of input transition time (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>) and load capacitance (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>), which can save the threshold crossing point (TCP) of the output waveform to better estimate the delay. However, the timing model is needed to reduce re-presentations, due to the high cost of building the library of ECSM. In this work, we present a timing model of the complete ECSM LUT for a CMOS inverter. The timing model is divided into two cases with a total of five regions. The proposed timing model is further analyzed by judging the value of threshold crossing points’ voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TCP</inf>) and drain to source saturation voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dsat</inf>), and the model is simplified for different threshold crossing points. Compared with the simulation results of HSPICE, the model is accurate with a maximum error of 2.35% and a maximum average error of 0.45%, which reduces the repetitive simulation of HSPICE.

articleTitle: A 1.8-V 1.9-ppm/°C 0.042% Inaccuracy CMOS Bandgap Reference with Curvature Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A high-precision bandgap reference (BGR) is proposed in this paper. A detail analysis of various error sources is provided. The non-PTAT errors are removed with the use of offset cancellation and curvature compensation technique, and the residual PTAT errors can be eliminated by a single room temperature trim. The proposed BGR is implemented in a 180nm CMOS process and the active area is 0.059m$\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The simulation results show that the temperature coefficient (TC) is 1.9 ppm/°C with a temperature range of −40-125°C. The variation coefficient σ/μ of the output voltage is 0.042%.

articleTitle: A Wideband Mixer with Adaptive Bias Current Adjustment Function
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A wideband mixer with adaptive bias current adjustment function based on 130nm SiGe BiCMOS process is presented in this paper, which is mainly composed of three modules: mixer core, power detection module, level shift circuit. By using the power detection module, the bias current of the mixer can be increased when there is a large signal input, resulting in higher linearity. The operating frequency of the wideband mixer is 0.9-6GHz, the results show that in the down-conversion mode with a high bias current, IPldB ranges from 10.2 to ll.ldBm, input IP3 ranges from 21 to 29dBm, and the power conversion gain is 0. 6∼1.47dB. The single-sideband noise figure is lower than 14.1dB.

articleTitle: Interconnect Reliability Simulation Analysis of Fan-out Package redistribution Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As a typical representative of advanced package, fan-out package has gradually become the main package form of advanced process chips, which has been widely used in consumer electronics and also has broad application prospects in high-reliability fields such as aviation, aerospace. Taking the fan-out package device as the research object, a finite element simulation model is established by ANSYS to evaluate the interconnection structure reliability of the redistribution layer under different geometrical parameters of the package. The simulation results are of great significance for the high reliability design and application of fan-out packages.

articleTitle: An Acceleration Architecture of Polynomial Multiplication based on NTT for CKKS Homomorphic Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: The Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) is currently widely used to accelerate polynomial multiplication in finite fields, which is the computational bottleneck of lattice-based fully homomorphic encryption schemes. The key challenge of NTT hardware structure implementation lies in the large amount of data storage and the complex pattern of data access. This paper proposes an efficient data access pattern of NTT algorithm. Benefiting from the specific pattern optimization of different stages of NTT, the use of hardware resource can be reduced by 46%~80%, and the performance based on FPGA is increased up to 4.9x compared with state-of-the-art NTT implementation. Furthermore, we apply the proposed hardware structure to realize the homomorphic evaluation of the CKKS homomorphic scheme, whose performance is improved by 7300x compared with software implementation.

articleTitle: RS-CIM: A Charge Domain Compute-in-Memory Architecture with Resolution Shifting ADC for Intelligent Perception Edge Nodes
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: For the intelligent perception nodes at the edge, analog Compute-in-Memory (CIM) is promising for its speed and power benefits, whereas Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs) are the bottleneck of performance and efficiency. This brief presents a CIM architecture with resolution shifting SAR ADC, namely RS-CIM. The multiply-accumulate (MAC) operation of signed numbers is completed in the form of charge-sharing, which significantly improves energy efficiency. By truncating and quantifying the dynamic range of the bit line, which represents the result of MAC, the signal margin of the least significant bit (LSB) expands. Meanwhile, a configurable shift operation restores the data range after quantification to compensate for the loss of accuracy caused by low-resolution ADC. Based on TSMC 40nm process, the RS-CIM is designed and verified. The simulation results show that the energy efficiency of RS-CIM can reach 326.5TOPS/W, and end-to-end classification accuracy on CIFAR-10 achieves 83.37%.

articleTitle: A 1.8V 109.3 dB SNDR Continuous Time Sigma-Delta Modulator for Audio Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: This paper describes a single-loop 3rd-order continuous time Sigma Delta modulator for audio applications in 180nm CMOS technology. It uses a feedforward topology structure that employs summation ahead technology to reduce circuit power consumption. Meanwhile, it adopts the Negative-R compensation technology to compensate the non-ideal factors of the active RC integrator, and the quantizer consists of a 3-bit flash ADC with low kickback noise dynamic comparator so that improve modulator resolution. The simulation results show that at 1. 8V supply voltage, the SNDR is 109.3 dB, the power consumption is 461.8$\mu$W, and the FOMSNDR is 185.7 dB.

articleTitle: A 6b/8b Configurable High-Speed Asynchronous SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A high-speed asynchronous successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with configurable resolution is realized. The SAR ADC is configurable to 6-bit mode with sampling rate up to 180 MS/s and 8-bit mode with 100 MS/s. Among the resolution switches, a novel symmetric structure switch is proposed to control the SAR ADC to realize 6-bit and 8-bit configurability and to reduce the effect of charge injection caused by DAC capacitor arrays and applications under low voltage conditions. The proposed SAR logic circuit uses monopole double throw switches to control the SAR ADC to realize high speed resolution configurable SAR ADC. In addition, asynchronous processing is used to improve the speed of the SAR ADC. The design is completed using 65nm CMOS process, and this simulation shows that the SAR ADC achieves INL and DNL of 0.04 LSB and 0.062 LSB in 6-bit mode at a voltage of 1.1 V. The effective number of bits (ENOB) is 5.717 bits in 6-bit mode and 7.129 bits in 8-bit mode. Signal-to-noise and distortion ratio (SNDR) in 6-bit and 8-bit modes is 36.18dB and 44.68dB, respectively.

articleTitle: CBi-GRU: Post-route timing path analysis method based on combined bidirectional GRU
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: As the level of circuit integration increases, the physical design becomes more and more complex, iterative static timing analysis(STA) is one of the most time-consuming task to achieve timing closure. After the route stage, fast and accurate timing analysis prediction can effectively reduce the number of static timing analysis in iterations, thereby improving design efficiency and reducing design cycle. In order to quickly predict the timing results after route, we propose a fast timing analysis predictor based on gate recurrent unit (GRU) neural network. This method extracts the features of combinations of cells and nets, assigns attention weights to different combinations, then predicts the hold slacks and setup slacks of each path in multi-corners. The experimental results in the sub-30nm show that the standard deviation of the prediction error ranges 5.41∼16.44ps, and the mean absolute error ranges 6.87∼18.55ps, and the prediction correlation is more than 0.96. Moreover, the speed of timing path prediction is more than 197 times faster than the analysis by STA tools, so that it can effectively and accurately accelerate the process of timing analysis and improve the efficiency of physical design.

articleTitle: An In-Situ Deep Learning-Based Defect Detection Technology for Additive Manufacturing Process
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: A trend in the additive manufacturing (AM) area is to deliver full-functional end-use products rather than discrete parts. Therefore, multiple manufacturing processes, additive or traditional, need to be combined to enable complex structure building, various material processing, and end-use functionality actualization. 3D electronics is a type of important product that such AM technologies can produce. However, the whole manufacturing procedure is much more complex than ever before, and any defect that occurs during this period may fail the product. To address the challenge, this paper proposes a deep learning-based defect detection technology to monitor the AM fabrication procedure in situ. An improved YOLOv8 algorithm is developed to train the defect detection model to identify and evaluate the defect image. A dataset of 3550 defects in four categories was created by selecting typical defects of the extrusion 3D printing process to testify to the practicability of this method. Experimental results showed that the improved YOLOv8 model achieves a mean average precision (mAP50) of 91.7% with a frame rate of 71.9 frames per second. In the future, this technology can be deployed on AM apparatus for real-time quality monitoring during the fabrication period. Moreover, depending on the detection results, printing settings can be adjusted real-timely to enhance the success rate of the printing process.

articleTitle: Voltage over Scaling for Approximate Newton Method in Total Variation-based Image Denoising
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Approximate computing is an energy efficient technique that allows acceptable errors to improve circuits' energy and latency performance in image processing. This paper presents a runtime-based approximate integrated method by applying the voltage over scaling (VOS) technique to the approximate Newton method for total variation (TV)-based image denoising. The proposed technique reduces the energy dissipation of the approximate Newton method by decreasing the supply voltage of adder cells. The output delay thus increases beyond the worst-case delay, thereby causing errors in the output; the number of output errors varies without changing the circuit structure. The results illustrate that the output image quality is kept constant when the number of approximate bits (NAB) is smaller than 15 for both exact and approximate cell using VOS; meanwhile, the energy consumption decreases gradually. When the NAB value is high at around NAB=17 with 50% noise, the exact full adder shows better performance than the approximate cell (AMA1) when the approximation is low (less than five errors); the maximum number of iterations and energy consumption for AMA1 (16.2 and 14.33nJ) is larger than for exact full adder (8.6 and 7.26nJ).

articleTitle: An Efficient Accelerator on FPGA for Large Convolution and Correlation using Winograd
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: FPGAs have become an attractive option for deep learning algorithms acceleration due to their reconfigurability and abundant logic resources. However, facing large kernel convolution and feature correlation, FPGA-based accelerators are often limited by on-chip DSP resources, making it difficult to cope with the exponentially increased computational load. To break through the limitation, we design the Winograd Accelerator Cores (WACs) to achieve efficient computation of convolution and correlation at the same time. To meet the bandwidth requirements of WACs with less FPGA resources, we propose an on-chip buffer system based on Line-Buffer and sliding registers. To maximize the usage of FPGA resources for computing while ensuring the scalability of accelerators on different FPGA devices, we propose a dataflow-driven multi-core accelerator architecture based on WACs. Finally, we implemented the accelerator using Xilinx Vivado HLS and deployed it on FPGA devices for performance evaluation to demonstrate the efficiency. On Xilinx xczu9eg, the actual performance can reach 1078.73GOPS, and the DSP utilization radio reaches 4.21. Its performance is more than 37.83% higher than that of Angel-Eye, and the DSP utilization ratio is 158.40% and 12.60% higher than that of Angel-Eye and Extended-DPU, respectively.

articleTitle: A Multi-channel LED Current Mismatch Calibration Method Based On PWM Duty Cycle and Amplitude Segmentation Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Microsystems (ICICM)
abstract: Brightness uniformity is an important indicator of backlight. In this paper, a current mismatch calibration method is proposed to improve the brightness uniformity of multichannel LEDs in LCD backlight applications. This method takes the advantage of the existing comparator and DAC within the LED driver chip to achieve current mismatch measurement, and calibrates the current mismatch by adjusting the PWM duty cycle. The measurement and calibration accuracy can be further improved by amplitude-segmented current output circuit. By adjusting the PWM duty cycle with the amplitude segmentation method for calibration, we can achieve ±0.16% current mismatch. The extensive results of mixed-signal simulation on 0.18$\mu$m BCD process show that this method can effectively improve the multi-channel LED current mismatch.
